nodes.name: Proof of Lemma (periodic bounded solutions)
nodes.statement: For $i\in\mathbb{Z}$, let $r(i)\in\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$ be its residue modulo $m$. Periodicity gives $ \Phi_A(k+m,\ell+m)=\Phi_A(k,\ell) $ and, writing $i=r(i)+qm$, we have \begin{equation} \Phi_A(k,i)=\Phi_A(k-i+r(i),r(i)). \end{equation} Consider the sequence \begin{equation} v_k:= \sum_{i \leq k}\Phi_A(k,i)P_{r(i)}w_{i} -\sum_{ i > k}\Phi_A(k,i)Q_{r(i)}w_{i}, \quad k \in \mathbb{Z}. \end{equation} Although the splitting need not be periodic, \eqref{eq:periodic-shift} allows us to use the projections at the representative indices $r(i)$. By \eqref{eq:periodic-shift} and {\rm(GH1*)}, {\rm(GH3*)}, \[ \|\Phi_A(k,i)P_{r(i)}\| \leq C^2\lambda^{k-i}, \qquad i\leq k, \] \[ \|\Phi_A(k,i)Q_{r(i)}\| \leq C^2\lambda^{i-k}, \qquad i>k. \] Hence the series in \eqref{eq:green-series} converge. Summing the geometric tail yields $|v_k| \leq L = C^{2}\frac{1+\lambda}{1-\lambda}$. Changing the summation index by $m$ and using \[ \Phi_A(k+m,i+m)=\Phi_A(k,i),\qquad r(i+m)=r(i),\qquad w_{i+m}=w_i, \] gives $v_{k+m}=v_k$. Moreover, using $ A_k\Phi_A(k,i)=\Phi_A(k+1,i) $ and $P_{r(k+1)}+Q_{r(k+1)}=Id$, direct cancellation in \eqref{eq:green-series} gives $ v_{k+1}=A_kv_k+w_{k+1}. $
nodes.statement_short: Green-type series using projections at representative indices r(i); periodicity of A gives periodic, bounded solutions.

nodes.name: Periodic shift identity (44)
nodes.statement: \Phi_A(k,i)=\Phi_A(k-i+r(i),r(i)).
nodes.label: eq:periodic-shift

nodes.name: Green-type series (45)
nodes.statement: v_k:= \sum_{i \leq k}\Phi_A(k,i)P_{r(i)}w_{i} -\sum_{ i > k}\Phi_A(k,i)Q_{r(i)}w_{i}, \quad k \in \mathbb{Z}.
nodes.label: eq:green-series

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma (robustness for sequences)
nodes.statement: Let $B_k = A_k + \Delta_k$. Denote $$ A_k = \begin{bmatrix} A_k^{ss} & A_k^{su} \\ A_k^{us} & A_k^{uu} \end{bmatrix} , \quad \Delta_k = \begin{bmatrix} \Delta_k^{ss} & \Delta_k^{su} \\ \Delta_k^{us} & \Delta_k^{uu} \end{bmatrix}, $$ where \begin{align*} A_k^{ss}: E_k^s \to E_{k+1}^s, & \quad A_k^{ss} = P_{k+1}A_k;& \qquad A_k^{su}: E_k^u \to E_{k+1}^s, & \quad A_k^{su} = P_{k+1}A_k;\\ A_k^{us}: E_k^s \to E_{k+1}^u, & \quad A_k^{us} = Q_{k+1}A_k;& \qquad A_k^{uu}: E_k^u \to E_{k+1}^u, & \quad A_k^{uu} = Q_{k+1}A_k, \end{align*} The operators $\Delta_k^{ss}$, $\Delta_k^{su}$, $\Delta_k^{us}$, and $\Delta_k^{uu}$ are defined in the same way, replacing $A_k$ by $\Delta_k$. By (GH2*) we have $A_k^{us}=0$, and therefore $$ A_k = \begin{bmatrix} A_k^{ss} & A_k^{su} \\ 0 & A_k^{uu} \end{bmatrix} $$ Denote $ F_k^u = A_k^{-1} E_{k+1}^u. $ By (GH2*) we have $F_k^u \subseteq E_k^u$, and the map $A_k:F_k^u \to E_{k+1}^u$ is a bijection. Therefore, it has an inverse; denote it by $Z_k: E_{k+1}^u \to F_k^u$, $$ Z_kA_k^{uu} = Id|_{F_k^u}, \quad A_k^{uu}Z_k = Id|_{E_{k+1}^u}, \quad Z_k = A_k^{-1}|_{E^u_{k+1}}. $$ Let us first prove item \textit{(Robust1)}. Denote $L' = 1+ C^2 \frac{\lambda^2}{1-\lambda^2}$. Fix $\varepsilon<1/(2R)$ sufficiently small so that, for \begin{equation} \varepsilon_1 = C\varepsilon, \quad \varepsilon_2 = 2L'R\varepsilon_1 \end{equation} the following inequality holds \begin{equation} R(2\varepsilon_1 + 2(R+\varepsilon_1)\varepsilon_2 + (R+\varepsilon_1)2\varepsilon_2) \leq \frac{1}{2L'}. \end{equation} Since $ \|A_k^{-1}(B_k-A_k)\|<\frac{1}{2}, $ each $B_k$ is an isomorphism and $ \|B_k^{-1}\|\leq 2R. $ In the following we show that there exists a sequence of linear maps $H_k: E_k^s \to F_k^u$, $\|H_k\| \leq \varepsilon_2$, such that for linear spaces \begin{equation} \tilde{E}_k^s = \{v_k^s+H_k v_k^s: \; v_k^s \in E_k^s\} \end{equation} holds the inclusion \begin{equation} B_k \tilde{E}_k^s \subseteq \tilde{E}_{k+1}^s. \end{equation} \begin{remark} In the standard robustness proof for exponential dichotomy, the latter inclusion is replaced by an equality, and the operators $H_k$ are assumed to act on $E_k^u$. These differences lead to the corresponding changes in the arguments. \end{remark} Consider the vectors $v_k^s \in E_k^s$ and $\tilde{v}_k^s = v_k^s + H_k v_k^s \in \tilde{E}_k^s$. The following holds \begin{multline*} B_k \tilde{v}_k^s = \left(\begin{bmatrix} A_k^{ss} & A_k^{su} \\ 0 & A_k^{uu} \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} \Delta_k^{ss} & \Delta_k^{su} \\ \Delta_k^{us} & \Delta_k^{uu} \end{bmatrix} \right) \begin{bmatrix} v_k^s \\ H_k v_k^s \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} A_k^{ss}v_k^s + A_k^{su}H_kv_k^s + \Delta_{k}^{ss}v_k^s + \Delta_k^{su} H_k v_k^s \\ A_k^{uu}H_kv_k^s + \Delta_k^{us}v_k^s + \Delta_k^{uu}H_k v_k^s \end{bmatrix}. \end{multline*} Inclusion $B_k \tilde{v}_k^s \in \tilde{E}_{k+1}^s$ is equivalent to equality $$ (H_{k+1}A_k^{ss} + H_{k+1}A_k^{su}H_k + H_{k+1}\Delta_k^{ss} + H_{k+1}\Delta_k^{su}H_k)v_k^s = (A_k^{uu}H_k + \Delta_k^{us} + \Delta_k^{uu}H_k)v_k^s. $$ \begin{statement} If a sequence of operators $H_k: E_k^s \to F_k^u$ satisfies \begin{equation} A_k^{uu}H_k = H_{k+1}A_k^{ss} - \Delta_k^{us} - \Delta_k^{uu}H_k + H_{k+1}A_k^{su}H_k + H_{k+1}\Delta_k^{ss} + H_{k+1}\Delta_k^{su}H_k \end{equation} then inclusions \eqref{eq:ETildaIncl} hold. \end{statement} Consider the following auxiliary problem. Given a sequence of bounded operators $S_k: E_k^s \to F_k^u$, we seek a bounded sequence of operators $H_k: E_k^s \to F_k^u$ that satisfies \begin{equation} H_k = Z_kH_{k+1}A_k^{ss} + S_k. \end{equation} Let $X$ be the Banach space of such operator sequences $\{S_k\}_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$ endowed with the norm $\|\{S_k\}\| = \sup_k \|S_k\|$. Consider the operator $F:X\to X$ defined by \begin{equation} F(\{S_k\}) = \{H_k\}, \quad \mbox{where} \quad H_k = S_k + \sum_{l = 1}^{+\infty}Z_k\cdot \ldots \cdot Z_{k+(l-1)}S_{k+l}A_{k+(l-1)}^{ss} \cdot \ldots \cdot A_k^{ss}. \end{equation} Due to condition (GH3*) for $l \geq 0$, the following inequalities hold $$ \|Z_k\cdot \ldots \cdot Z_{k+(l-1)}\| \leq C \lambda^l, \quad \|A_{k+(l-1)}^{ss}\cdot \ldots \cdot A_k^{ss}\| \leq C \lambda^l. $$ Hence, the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:defFHk} converges and \begin{equation} \|F(\{S_k\})\| \leq \|\{S_k\}\| \left(1+ \sum_{l=1}^{\infty} C^2\lambda^{2l} \right) = \|\{S_k\}\|\left(1+ C^2 \frac{\lambda^2}{1-\lambda^2}\right) = L' \|\{S_k\}\|. \end{equation} A straightforward substitution shows that $H_k$, $S_k$ satisfy \eqref{eq:HkSk}. Consider the nonlinear operator $Q:X \to X$ defined as $Q(\{H_k\}) = \{S_k\}$, where $$ S_k = Z_k(- \Delta_k^{us} - \Delta_k^{uu}H_k + H_{k+1}A_k^{su}H_k + H_{k+1}\Delta_k^{ss} + H_{k+1}\Delta_k^{su}H_k). $$ Note that if $\{H_k\} \in X$ is a fixed point of $F \circ Q$, i.e. $\{H_k\} = F \circ Q (\{H_k\})$, then $\{H_k\}$ satisfies~\eqref{eq:StHk}. Let $\varepsilon_2$ satisfy the conditions \eqref{eq:condep1ep2}. Let $U$ be the closed ball in $X$ of radius $\varepsilon_2$ centered at $0$. In the following, we show that $F \circ Q : U \to U$ and $F \circ Q|_{U}$ is a contraction. Consider $H = \{H_k\}, H' = \{H'_k\} \in U$, and assume that $ \|H_k\|, \|H'_k\| \leq \varepsilon_2$, $\|H-H'\| = \delta $. Let us estimate $Q\{H_k\} - Q\{H'_k\} = \{S_k - S'_k\}$. The following holds \begin{multline*} \|S_k - S'_k\| \leq \|Z_k\| \cdot \|-\Delta_k^{uu}(H_k-H_k') + H_{k+1}A_k^{su}H_k -H'_{k+1}A_k^{su}H'_k + \\ (H_{k+1}-H'_{k+1})\Delta_k^{ss} + H_{k+1}\Delta_k^{su}H_k - H'_{k+1}\Delta_k^{su}H'_k\| \leq \\ R(2\varepsilon_1 \delta + (H_{k+1}-H'_{k+1})(A_k^{su}+\Delta_k^{su})H_k + H_{k+1}(A_k^{su}+\Delta_k^{su})(H_k-H'_k) \\ - (H_{k+1}-H'_{k+1})(A_k^{su}+\Delta_k^{su})(H_k-H'_k)) \leq \\ R(2 \varepsilon_1 \delta + 2\delta(R+\varepsilon_1)\varepsilon_2 + (R+\varepsilon_1)\delta^2 ) = R(2\varepsilon_1 + 2(R+\varepsilon_1)\varepsilon_2 + (R+\varepsilon_1)\delta)\delta. \end{multline*} Taking into account \eqref{eq:condep1ep2} and $\delta \leq 2\varepsilon_2$ we conclude that $ \|QH - QH'\| \leq \frac{1}{2L'}\|H-H'\|. $ Since $F$ is linear, inequality \eqref{eq:FL'} implies that \begin{equation} \|F \circ QH - F \circ QH'\| \leq L'\frac{1}{2L'}\|H-H'\| = \frac{1}{2}\|H-H'\|, \end{equation} and hence $F \circ Q$ is contracting on $U$. Note that $\|Q\{H_k = 0\}\| = \|\{-Z_k\Delta_k^{us}\}\| \leq R\varepsilon_1$, hence $ \|F \circ Q\{H_k = 0\}\| \leq L'R\varepsilon_1 $ and according to \eqref{eq:FQcontr} and \eqref{eq:defep1ep2} for any $H \in U$ we have $$ \|F \circ Q H\| \leq \|F\circ QH-F\circ Q\{0\}\|+\|F\circ Q\{0\}\| \leq \varepsilon_2/2 + L'R\varepsilon_1 \leq \varepsilon_2 $$ and hence $F \circ Q(U) \subset U$. By the contraction mapping principle, there exists a unique $H = \{H_k\}$, with $|H_k| \leq \varepsilon_2$ such that $F \circ Q H = H$. Consequently, the subspaces $\tilde{E}_k^s$ defined by \eqref{eq:tildeEDef} satisfy \eqref{eq:ETildaIncl}. Let us show that for small enough $\varepsilon, \varepsilon_2$ the spaces $\tilde{E}_k^s$ satisfy \begin{equation} |B_{k+n-1} \cdot \ldots \cdot B_k\tilde{v}^s_k| \leq C_1 \lambda_1^n |\tilde{v}^s_k|, \quad \tilde{v}^s_k \in \tilde{E}^s_k, n \geq 0 \end{equation} for some $C_1 = C_1(C, \lambda, \lambda_1, R)$. Indeed, let us choose $N$ such that $2C\lambda^N \leq \lambda_1^N$ and choose $C_1 = \left(\frac{R+1}{\lambda_1}\right)^N$. For small enough $\varepsilon, \varepsilon_2$ we have $$ \|B_{k+N-1} \cdot \ldots \cdot B_k|_{\tilde{E}_k^s}\| \leq 2 \|A_{k+N-1} \cdot \ldots \cdot A_k|_{{E}_k^s}\| \leq 2C\lambda^N \leq \lambda_1^N, \quad k \in \mathbb{Z}. $$ Represent $n > 0$ in the form $n = lN + r$, with $l \geq 0$, $r \in [0, N-1]$. Note that \begin{multline} \|B_{k+n-1} \cdot \ldots \cdot B_k|_{\tilde{E}_k^s}\| \leq \\ \left(\prod_{i = 0}^{l-1}\|B_{k+(i+1)N-1} \cdot \ldots \cdot B_{k+iN}|_{\tilde{E}_{k+iN}^s}\|\right)\|B_{k+lN+r-1} \cdot \ldots \cdot B_{k+lN}|_{\tilde{E}_{k+lN}^s}\| \leq \\ (\lambda_1^N)^l(R+1)^r\leq C_1\lambda_1^n, \end{multline} which implies \eqref{eq:GH3Bs}. Similarly, for small enough $\varepsilon$ we construct a sequence of operators $H_k^u:E_k^u \to A_{k-1}E_{k-1}^s$ and spaces $\tilde{E}_k^u = \{ v_k^u + H_k^uv_k^u : v_k^u \in E_k^u\}$ such that $ B_k^{-1} \tilde{E}_{k+1}^u \subseteq \tilde{E}_{k}^u $ and \begin{equation} |B_{k-n}^{-1} \cdot \ldots \cdot B_{k-1}^{-1}\tilde{v}^u_k| \leq C_1 \lambda_1^n |\tilde{v}^u_k|, \quad \tilde{v}^u_k \in \tilde{E}^u_k, n \geq 0. \end{equation} For small enough $\varepsilon_2$ the inequalities $\|H_k\|, \|H_k^u\| \leq \varepsilon_2$ imply that the operator \begin{equation}\notag T_k = \begin{bmatrix} Id & H_k^u \\ H_k & Id \end{bmatrix} \end{equation} is invertible, and projections $ P_{\tilde{E}_{k}^{s, u}} = T_k\circ P_{{E}_k^{s, u}} \circ T^{-1}_{k} $ satisfy $\|P_{\tilde{E}_{k}^{s, u}}\| \leq 2C$ and $\tilde{E}_k^s \oplus \tilde{E}_k^u = \mathbb{B}$. Hence, the sequence $\mathcal{B}$ satisfies generalized hyperbolicity with spaces $\tilde{E}_k^s, \tilde{E}_k^u$ and constants $C_1, \lambda_1$. Item \textit{(Robust1)} is proved. To prove item \textit{(Robust2)}, we consider an $m$-periodic sequence of operators $\mathcal{A} = \{A_k\}$ that satisfies periodic generalized hyperbolicity, with the corresponding periodic splitting $\mathbb{B} = E_k^s \oplus E_k^u$. Let $\mathcal{B} = \{B_k\}$ be an $m$-periodic perturbation of $\mathcal{A}$ satisfying \eqref{eq:AkBk}. We show that the subspaces $\tilde{E}_k^s$, $\tilde{E}_k^u$ constructed in the proof of \textit{(Robust1)} are $m$-periodic. The sequence of operators $H = \{H_k\} \in X$ satisfying $(F \circ Q)H = H$ can be obtained as a limit of iterates $H^l = (F \circ Q)^l\{H_k = 0\} \in X$: $ H = \lim_{l \to \infty}H^l. $ If sequences $\mathcal{A}$, $\mathcal{B}$ and projections $P_k$, $Q_k$ are $m$-periodic, then the operator $(F \circ Q)$ maps $m$-periodic sequences to $m$-periodic sequences. Hence, for any $l>0$ the iterate $H^l$ is $m$-periodic, and so is its limit $H$. Therefore, the subspaces $\tilde{E}_k^s$ constructed in the proof of item \textit{(Robust1)} are $m$-periodic. Similar considerations show that $\tilde{E}_k^u$ is $m$-periodic as well. Consequently, $\mathcal{B}$ satisfies periodic generalized hyperbolicity. This proves item \textit{(Robust2)}.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma (finite Lipschitz shadowing)
nodes.statement: Let $M = 2L$. Fix $d_0 > 0$, satisfying the following inequalities \begin{equation} L + 2(RM+R)(RM+R+L)\cdot r\left((RM+R+L)d_0\right) \leq M, \end{equation} \begin{equation} 2 (RM+R+L) \cdot r\left((RM+R+L)d_0\right) < 1. \end{equation} We first prove the statement for intervals of the form $[-N,N]$. \begin{lem} For any $d < d_0$ and any $d$-pseudotrajectory $\{y_k\}_{k \in [-N, N]}$ there exists an exact trajectory $\{x_k\}_{k \in [-N, N]}$ such that $ |y_k - x_k| \leq Md $. \end{lem} \begin{proof} We prove the claim by induction on $N$. For $N=0$, the statement is immediate. Consider a $d$-pseudotrajectory $\{y_{k \in [-(N+1), N+1]}\}$ with $d<d_0$. By the induction hypothesis, the $d$-pseudotrajectory $\{y_{k \in [-N, N]}\}$ is $Md$-shadowed by an exact trajectory $\{p_{k \in [-N, N]}\}$ \begin{equation} |y_k - p_k| \leq M d, \quad k \in [-N, N]. \end{equation} Note that $p_{N+1} = f(p_N)$, $p_{-(N+1)} = f^{-1}(p_{-N})$. Due to \eqref{eq:C1-2}, \eqref{eq:pst1}, \eqref{eq:pst2} the following estimates hold \begin{equation} |y_{N+1} - p_{N+1}| \leq (RM+1)d, \quad |y_{-(N+1)} - p_{-(N+1)}| \leq (RM+R)d. \end{equation} Hence, we conclude the following. \begin{statement} For $d< d_0$ a $d$-pseudotrajectory $\{y_{k \in [-(N+1), N+1]}\}$ can be $(RM+R)d$-shadowed. \end{statement} In the following, we show how to construct a better shadowing trajectory. Denote $A_k = Df(p_k)$. Consider the sequence $\{w_k \in \mathbb{B}\}$ defined by $$ y_{k+1} - f(y_k) = - d w_{k+1}, \quad k \in [-(N+1), N], $$ $$ w_{k+1} = 0, \quad k \notin [-(N+1), N]. $$ Note that $|w_k| \leq 1$. By Lemma \ref{lem:SBS} there exists a sequence $\{v_k \in \mathbb{B}\}_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$, $|v_k| \leq L$ such that equalities \eqref{eq:Inh} hold. Consider the sequence $z_k = y_k + dv_k$. Note that $$ f(z_k) = f(y_k + dv_k) = f(p_k + (y_k-p_k) +dv_k), \quad k \in [-(N+1), N+1]. $$ Inequalities \eqref{eq:C1-1}, \eqref{eq:C1-2}, \eqref{Add4.1}, \eqref{Add4.2} imply that \begin{multline*} |f(z_k) - (f(p_k) + A_k (y_k - p_k + dv_k) )| \leq |y_k - p_k + dv_k|r(|y_k - p_k + dv_k|) \leq \\ (RM+R+L)d \cdot r\left((RM+R+L)d\right). \end{multline*} Then for $k \in [-(N+1), N]$ the following inequalities hold \begin{multline*} |z_{k+1} - f(z_k)| = |y_{k+1} + dv_{k+1} - p_{k+1} - \\ A_k (y_k - p_k + dv_k) - (f(z_k) - (f(p_k) + A_k (y_k - p_k + dv_k) ))| \leq \\ |y_{k+1} - p_{k+1} + dw_{k+1} - A_k (y_k - p_k)| +|f(z_k) - (f(p_k) + A_k (y_k - p_k + dv_k) )| \leq \\ |f(y_k) - f(p_k) - A_k (y_k - p_k)| + (RM+R+L)d \cdot r\left((RM+R+L)d\right) \leq \\ |y_k - p_k|r(|y_k - p_k|) + (RM+R+L)d \cdot r\left((RM+R+L)d\right) \leq \\ (RM+R)d\cdot r((RM+R)d) + (RM+R+L)d \cdot r\left((RM+R+L)d\right) \leq \\ 2 (RM+R+L)d \cdot r\left((RM+R+L)d\right). \end{multline*} Hence $\{z_{k \in [-(N+1), N+1]}\}$ is a $2 (RM+R+L)d \cdot r\left((RM+R+L)d\right)$-pseudotrajectory. Inequality~\eqref{eq:M2''} implies $ 2 (RM+R+L)d \cdot r\left((RM+R+L)d\right) < d_0 $. According to Proposition \ref{stat:dn+1} the pseudotrajectory $\{z_{k \in [-(N+1), N+1]}\}$ can be $2(RM+R)(RM+R+L)d \cdot r\left((RM+R+L)d\right)$-shadowed by an exact trajectory $q_{k \in [-(N+1), N+1]}$. Then by \eqref{eq:M2'} \begin{multline*} |y_k - q_k| \leq |y_k - z_k| + |z_k-q_k| \leq \\ Ld + 2(RM+R)(RM+R+L)d \cdot r\left((RM+R+L)d\right) \leq Md \end{multline*} and the pseudotrajectory $\{y_{k \in [-(N+1), N+1]}\}$ is $Md$-shadowed by $\{q_{k \in [-(N+1), N+1]}\}$, which completes the induction step and proves Lemma \ref{lem:NLipSh}. \end{proof} Every finite interval $I\subset\mathbb{Z}$ is contained in $[-N,N]$ for some $N>0$. Restricting the trajectory supplied by Lemma~\ref{lem:NLipSh} to $I$ proves Lemma~\ref{lem:FinLipSh}.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma (symmetric intervals)
nodes.statement: We prove the claim by induction on $N$. For $N=0$, the statement is immediate. Consider a $d$-pseudotrajectory $\{y_{k \in [-(N+1), N+1]}\}$ with $d<d_0$. By Lemma \ref{lem:SBS} there exists a sequence $\{v_k \in \mathbb{B}\}_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$, $|v_k| \leq L$ such that equalities \eqref{eq:Inh} hold. Consider the sequence $z_k = y_k + dv_k$. Note that $$ f(z_k) = f(y_k + dv_k) = f(p_k + (y_k-p_k) +dv_k), \quad k \in [-(N+1), N+1]. $$ Inequalities \eqref{eq:C1-1}, \eqref{eq:C1-2}, \eqref{Add4.1}, \eqref{Add4.2} imply that \begin{multline*} |f(z_k) - (f(p_k) + A_k (y_k - p_k + dv_k) )| \leq |y_k - p_k + dv_k|r(|y_k - p_k + dv_k|) \leq \\ (RM+R+L)d \cdot r\left((RM+R+L)d\right). \end{multline*} Then for $k \in [-(N+1), N]$ the following inequalities hold \begin{multline*} |z_{k+1} - f(z_k)| = |y_{k+1} + dv_{k+1} - p_{k+1} - \\ A_k (y_k - p_k + dv_k) - (f(z_k) - (f(p_k) + A_k (y_k - p_k + dv_k) ))| \leq \\ |y_{k+1} - p_{k+1} + dw_{k+1} - A_k (y_k - p_k)| +|f(z_k) - (f(p_k) + A_k (y_k - p_k + dv_k) )| \leq \\ |f(y_k) - f(p_k) - A_k (y_k - p_k)| + (RM+R+L)d \cdot r\left((RM+R+L)d\right) \leq \\ |y_k - p_k|r(|y_k - p_k|) + (RM+R+L)d \cdot r\left((RM+R+L)d\right) \leq \\ (RM+R)d\cdot r((RM+R)d) + (RM+R+L)d \cdot r\left((RM+R+L)d\right) \leq \\ 2 (RM+R+L)d \cdot r\left((RM+R+L)d\right). \end{multline*} Hence $\{z_{k \in [-(N+1), N+1]}\}$ is a $2 (RM+R+L)d \cdot r\left((RM+R+L)d\right)$-pseudotrajectory. According to Proposition \ref{stat:dn+1} the pseudotrajectory $\{z_{k \in [-(N+1), N+1]}\}$ can be $2(RM+R)(RM+R+L)d \cdot r\left((RM+R+L)d\right)$-shadowed by an exact trajectory $q_{k \in [-(N+1), N+1]}$. Then by \eqref{eq:M2'} \begin{multline*} |y_k - q_k| \leq |y_k - z_k| + |z_k-q_k| \leq \\ Ld + 2(RM+R)(RM+R+L)d \cdot r\left((RM+R+L)d\right) \leq Md \end{multline*} and the pseudotrajectory $\{y_{k \in [-(N+1), N+1]}\}$ is $Md$-shadowed by $\{q_{k \in [-(N+1), N+1]}\}$, which completes the induction step and proves Lemma \ref{lem:NLipSh}.

nodes.name: Bounded solution property implies Lipschitz shadowing
nodes.statement: Assume that $f:\mathbb{B}\to\mathbb{B}$ is a $C^1$-diffeomorphism satisfying \eqref{eq:C1-1}-\eqref{eq:C1-r2}, and that there exists $d_1, M > 0$ such that, for any $d < d_1$ and any $d$-pseudotrajectory $\{y_k\}$, the sequence ${\mathcal{B}} = \{B_k = Df(y_k)\}_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$ satisfies the bounded solution property with constant $M$. Then $f$ satisfies the Lipschitz shadowing property.
assumptions: Assume that $f:\mathbb{B}\to\mathbb{B}$ is a $C^1$-diffeomorphism satisfying \eqref{eq:C1-1}-\eqref{eq:C1-r2}
for any $d < d_1$ and any $d$-pseudotrajectory $\{y_k\}$, the sequence ${\mathcal{B}} = \{B_k = Df(y_k)\}_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$ satisfies the bounded solution property with constant $M$
conclusions: Then $f$ satisfies the Lipschitz shadowing property.
nodes.label: lem:BS-SH

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma (bounded solutions imply shadowing)
nodes.statement: By \eqref{eq:C1-r2} there exists $d_0 \in (0, d_1)$ such that \begin{equation} M\cdot r(Md_0) < \frac{1}{2}. \end{equation} \begin{statement} For $d_0$ satisfying \eqref{eq:1.1'} and any $d$-pseudotrajectory $\{y_k\}_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$ with $d<d_0$ there exists $d/2$-pseudotrajectory $\{z_k\}_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$ such that \begin{equation} |y_k-z_k| < Md. \end{equation} \end{statement} \begin{proof} Consider a $d$-pseudotrajectory $\{y_k\}$ with $d < d_0$. Similarly to the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:FinLipSh} consider the sequence $\{w_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}\}$ defined by \begin{equation} y_{k+1}-f(y_k) = -dw_{k+1}, \quad k \in \mathbb{Z}. \end{equation} Consider $B_k = Df(y_k)$. By the assumptions of Lemma \ref{lem:BS-SH} there exists a sequence $v_k \in \mathbb{B}$ such that $$ v_{k+1} - B_kv_k = w_{k+1}, \quad |v_k| \leq M, \quad k \in \mathbb{Z}. $$ Consider the sequence $\{z_k = y_k + dv_k\}_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$. By construction, $\{z_k\}$ satisfies \eqref{eq:d2}. We now show that $\{z_k\}$ is a $d/2$-pseudotrajectory. By the construction of the sequence $\{v_k\}$ we have \begin{equation} y_{k+1} + dv_{k+1} - (f(y_k) + B_kdv_k) = 0. \end{equation} Due to \eqref{eq:C1-1}, \eqref{eq:1.1'} and \eqref{eq:zkBk} the following inequalities hold \begin{multline*} |z_{k+1} - f(z_k)| = |y_{k+1} + dv_{k+1} - (f(y_k)+B_kdv_k) - (f(y_k+dv_k) - f(y_k) -B_kdv_k)| = \\ |f(y_k+dv_k) - f(y_k) -B_kdv_k| \leq d|v_k|r(d|v_k|) \leq Md \cdot r(Md) \leq \frac{d}{2}. \end{multline*} Proposition \ref{stat:d2} is proved. \end{proof} Continue the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:BS-SH}. For a given $d$-pseudotrajectory $\{y_k\}_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$ with $d< d_0$ consider the sequence of $\delta_l$-pseudotrajectories $\{y_k^l\}_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$ defined inductively. Define $\delta_0 = d$, $\{y_k^0 = y_k\}_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$. By a given $\delta_l$-pseudotrajectory $\{y_k^l\}_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$ with $\delta_l < d_0$ according to Proposition \ref{stat:d2} choose $\delta_{l+1} = \delta_l/2$-pseudotrajectory $\{y_k^{l+1}\}$ such that $ |y_k^{l+1} - y_k^l| \leq M \delta_l. $ By construction we have $\delta_l = \frac{d}{2^l}$ and \begin{equation} |y_{k+1}^l - f(y_k^l)| \leq \frac{d}{2^l}, \quad |y_k^{l+1} - y_k^l| \leq M\frac{d}{2^l}. \end{equation} Hence, for any fixed $k \in \mathbb{Z}$, the sequence $\{y_k^l\}$ is a Cauchy sequence with respect to $l$ and there exists a limit $ x_k = \lim_{l \to \infty} y_k^l. $ Note that \begin{equation} |y_k - x_k| = |y_k^0 - x_k| \leq \sum_{l\geq 0} |y_k^l-y_k^{l+1}| \leq \sum_{l\geq 0}M\frac{d}{2^l} = 2Md. \end{equation} The continuity of $f$ and condition \eqref{eq:3.1-3.2} imply that $x_{k+1} = f(x_k)$. Therefore, $\{x_k\}$ is an exact trajectory of $f$ that $2Md$-shadows $\{y_k\}$. Lemma \ref{lem:BS-SH} is proved.
nodes.statement_short: Error halving: each d-pseudotrajectory is Md-close to a d/2-pseudotrajectory; iterate and pass to the limit of a Cauchy sequence.

nodes.name: Proof of the error-halving step
nodes.statement: Consider a $d$-pseudotrajectory $\{y_k\}$ with $d < d_0$. Similarly to the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:FinLipSh} consider the sequence $\{w_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}\}$ defined by \begin{equation} y_{k+1}-f(y_k) = -dw_{k+1}, \quad k \in \mathbb{Z}. \end{equation} Consider $B_k = Df(y_k)$. By the assumptions of Lemma \ref{lem:BS-SH} there exists a sequence $v_k \in \mathbb{B}$ such that $$ v_{k+1} - B_kv_k = w_{k+1}, \quad |v_k| \leq M, \quad k \in \mathbb{Z}. $$ Consider the sequence $\{z_k = y_k + dv_k\}_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$. By construction, $\{z_k\}$ satisfies \eqref{eq:d2}. We now show that $\{z_k\}$ is a $d/2$-pseudotrajectory. By the construction of the sequence $\{v_k\}$ we have \begin{equation} y_{k+1} + dv_{k+1} - (f(y_k) + B_kdv_k) = 0. \end{equation} Due to \eqref{eq:C1-1}, \eqref{eq:1.1'} and \eqref{eq:zkBk} the following inequalities hold \begin{multline*} |z_{k+1} - f(z_k)| = |y_{k+1} + dv_{k+1} - (f(y_k)+B_kdv_k) - (f(y_k+dv_k) - f(y_k) -B_kdv_k)| = \\ |f(y_k+dv_k) - f(y_k) -B_kdv_k| \leq d|v_k|r(d|v_k|) \leq Md \cdot r(Md) \leq \frac{d}{2}. \end{multline*} Proposition \ref{stat:d2} is proved.

nodes.name: Normalized errors w_k (64)
nodes.statement: y_{k+1}-f(y_k) = -dw_{k+1}, \quad k \in \mathbb{Z}.
nodes.label: eq:defw

nodes.name: Halving estimates (66)
nodes.statement: |y_{k+1}^l - f(y_k^l)| \leq \frac{d}{2^l}, \quad |y_k^{l+1} - y_k^l| \leq M\frac{d}{2^l}.
nodes.label: eq:3.1-3.2

nodes.name: Total displacement (67)
nodes.statement: |y_k - x_k| = |y_k^0 - x_k| \leq \sum_{l\geq 0} |y_k^l-y_k^{l+1}| \leq \sum_{l\geq 0}M\frac{d}{2^l} = 2Md.
nodes.label: eq:42.5

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem (M1): Lipschitz shadowing
nodes.statement: Now we show that the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:main-results}\,(\ref{item:main-LipSh}) imply the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:BS-SH}. By Lemma \ref{lem:FinLipSh}, the map $f$ satisfies the finite Lipschitz shadowing property. Let $L > 0$ be the constant from Lemma \ref{lem:SBS}, let $\varepsilon > 0$ be the constant from Lemma \ref{lem:SBS-robust}, and let $M, d_0$ be the constants from the finite Lipschitz shadowing property. By condition \eqref{eq:C1-r1}, choose $\delta > 0$ such that if $|x - y|< \delta$ we have $\|Df(x)-Df(y)\| < \varepsilon$. Set $d_1 := \min(d_0, \delta/M)$. Fix $d<d_1$ and a $d$-pseudotrajectory $\{y_k\}_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$. Define the sequence of operators $\mathcal{B} = \{B_k = Df(y_k)\}_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$. We claim that the sequence $\mathcal{B}$ satisfies the bounded solution property with constant $4L$. By Lemma \ref{lem:FinLipSh}, for any finite interval $I \subset \mathbb{Z}$ the sequence $\{y_k\}_{k \in I}$ can be $Md$-shadowed by an exact trajectory $\{x_k\}_{k \in I}$. Set $\{A_k = Df(x_k)\}_{k \in I}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:SBS} it satisfies the strong bounded solution property with constant $L$. Moreover, since $Md < \delta$ we have $\|B_k - A_k\| \leq \varepsilon$, $k \in I$. By Lemma \ref{lem:SBS-robust}, the sequence $\{B_k\}_{k \in I}$ satisfies the bounded solution property with constant~$2L$. Lemma~\ref{lem:Bk-Inf} implies that $\{B_k\}_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$ satisfies the bounded solution property with constant~$4L$. Therefore, the hypotheses of Lemma \ref{lem:BS-SH} hold, which completes the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:main-results}\,(\ref{item:main-LipSh}).
nodes.statement_short: Verify the hypothesis of the bounded-solutions lemma: finite shadowing, strong bounded solutions along exact orbits, robustness, and finite-to-infinite extension give constant 4L.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem (M2): Lipschitz periodic shadowing
nodes.statement: Let $\{y_k\}$ be an $m$-periodic $d$-pseudotrajectory. By Theorem~\ref{thm:main-results}\,(\ref{item:main-LipSh}), there exists $M > 0$ such that $\{y_k\}$ is $Md$-shadowed by an exact trajectory (not necessarily periodic) $\{x_k\}$: $$ \mathrm{dist}(y_k, x_k) \leq Md, \quad k \in \mathbb{Z}. $$ Define the sequences of the linear maps $\mathcal{B} = \{B_k := Df(y_k)\}$ and $\mathcal{A} = \{A_k := Df(x_k)\}$. Since $f$ satisfies generalized hyperbolicity, the sequence $\mathcal{A}$ satisfies generalized hyperbolicity as well. By item (Robust1) of Lemma~\ref{lem:CL-robust-Ak}, for any $\lambda_1 \in (\lambda, 1)$ there exists $C_1 = C_1(C, \lambda, \lambda_1, R) > 0$ such that, for sufficiently small $d$, the sequence $\mathcal{B}$ also satisfies generalized hyperbolicity with constants $C_1$, $\lambda_1$. Consider the $m$-periodic sequence $\{w_k \in \mathbb{B}\}$ defined by~\eqref{eq:defw}. By Lemma~\ref{lem:SBS-periodic}, there exist $L = L(C_1, \lambda_1) > 0$ and an $m$-periodic sequence $\{v_k \in \mathbb{B}\}$ such that $$ v_{k+1} = B_k v_k + w_{k+1}, \quad \text{and} \quad \|v_k\| \leq L. $$ Using an argument as in Proposition~\ref{stat:d2}, and reducing $d$ if necessary, there exists a constant $M_1 > 0$ such that the sequence $y_k^1 := y_k + d v_k$, $k \in \mathbb{Z}$, is an $m$ -periodic $d/2$ -pseudotrajectory and, furthermore, satisfies $\|y_k - y_k^1\| \leq M_1 d$. By iterating this construction, as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:main-results}\,(\ref{item:main-LipSh}), we obtain a sequence of $m$-periodic pseudotrajectories $\{y_k^l\}_{l \geq 1}$ satisfying the following estimates (compare with~\eqref{eq:3.1-3.2}): $$ \|y_{k+1}^l - f(y_k^l)\| \leq \frac{d}{2^l}, \quad \|y_k^{l+1} - y_k^l\| \leq M_1 \frac{d}{2^l}. $$ Taking the pointwise limit $z_k := \lim_{l \to \infty} y_k^l$, we obtain an $m$-periodic exact trajectory, similarly to~\eqref{eq:42.5}, satisfying $ \|y_k - z_k\| \leq 2M_1 d. $ This completes the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:main-results}\,(\ref{item:main-LipPerSh}).
nodes.statement_short: Shadow by a not necessarily periodic orbit, deduce GH of the periodic differentials by robustness, then iterate periodic bounded-solution corrections.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem (M3): density of periodic points
nodes.statement: Let $M, d_0 > 0$ be the constants from the Lipschitz periodic shadowing property in Theorem~\ref{thm:main-results}\,(\ref{item:main-LipPerSh}). Fix $x \in CR(f)$. For any $d \in (0, d_0)$ consider a finite pseudotrajectory $y_{k \in [0, N]}$ such that $y_0 = y_N = x$. This segment can be continued to an $N$-periodic pseudotrajectory $$ y_{k+iN} = y_k, \quad k \in [0, N-1], i \in \mathbb{Z}. $$ By Theorem~\ref{thm:main-results}\,(\ref{item:main-LipPerSh}) there exists an $N$-periodic exact trajectory $x_k^{(d)}$ that $Md$-shadows $\{y_k\}$; in particular $ |x - x_0^{(d)}| = |y_0 - x_0^{(d)}| \leq Md $. Since $x_0^{(d)} \in Per(f)$ it follows that $\overline{Per(f)} = CR(f)$.
nodes.statement_short: Close a chain from x to x into a periodic pseudotrajectory and shadow it by a periodic orbit within Md.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem (M4): uniform C^1 robustness
nodes.statement: The proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:main-results}\,(\ref{item:main-robust}) combines Theorem~\ref{thm:main-results}\,(\ref{item:main-LipSh})--(\ref{item:main-LipPerSh}) with the robustness of generalized hyperbolicity for sequences of operators (Lemma~\ref{lem:CL-robust-Ak}). Indeed, consider a diffeomorphism $f:\mathbb{B} \to \mathbb{B}$ satisfying generalized hyperbolicity with constants $C, \lambda$. Fix $\lambda_1 \in (\lambda, 1)$. For any trajectory $\{x_k\}$, the sequence of linear operators $\{Df(x_k)\}$ satisfies generalized hyperbolicity. Take $M, d_0 > 0$ as in Theorem~\ref{thm:main-results}\, (\ref{item:main-LipSh})--(\ref{item:main-LipPerSh}) and $\varepsilon > 0, C_1 > C$ provided by Lemma~\ref{lem:CL-robust-Ak}. Choose $\delta \in (0, \min(d_0, \varepsilon/2))$ such that \begin{equation} \|Df(x)-Df(y)\| \leq \varepsilon/2, \quad |x-y| < M\delta. \end{equation} Let $g\in\mathfrak{D}(\mathbb{B})$ satisfy \begin{equation} \|f-g\|_{C^1}<\delta. \end{equation} Consider the set $\mathcal{O}$ of all trajectories of the diffeomorphism $g$. For any trajectory $\omega \in \mathcal{O}$ choose a point $y_{\omega} \in \omega$. We now construct spaces $E_y^{s, u}$ for all points $y \in \omega$. Consider an exact trajectory $y_{k\in \mathbb{Z}}$ of diffeomorphism $g$ with $y_0 = y_{\omega}$. Note that $|y_{k+1} - f(y_k)| = |g(y_k) - f(y_k)| \leq \delta$, $k \in \mathbb{Z}$, hence $y_k$ is a $\delta$-pseudotrajectory of the diffeomorphism $f$. Denote $B_k = Dg(y_k)$. Consider two cases. \textbf{Case 1.} If the sequence $\{y_{k}\}$ is not periodic, then the points $\{y_k\}$ are pairwise distinct. By Theorem~\ref{thm:main-results}\,(\ref{item:main-LipSh}) there exists an exact trajectory $\{x_k\}$ of diffeomorphism $f$ that $M\delta$-shadows~$\{y_k\}$: \begin{equation} |y_k-x_k| \leq M\delta, \quad x_{k+1} = f(x_k), \quad k \in \mathbb{Z}. \end{equation} Denote $A_k = Df(x_k)$. According to \eqref{eq:delta1}, \eqref{eq:delta2} the following holds \begin{equation} \|A_k - B_k\| \leq \|A_k - Df(y_k)\| + \|Df(y_k) - B_k\| \leq \varepsilon/2 + \delta < \varepsilon. \end{equation} By item (Robust1) in Lemma \ref{lem:CL-robust-Ak}, the sequence $\{B_k\}$ satisfies generalized hyperbolicity with constants $C_1, \lambda_1$. \textbf{Case 2.} Suppose that the sequence $\{y_{k}\}$ is $m$-periodic. Then the sequence $\{B_k\}$ is $m$-periodic as well. By Theorem~\ref{thm:main-results}\,(\ref{item:main-LipPerSh}), there exists an $m$-periodic exact trajectory $\{x_k\}$ satisfying \eqref{eq:robustykxk}. The sequence $\{A_k = Df(x_k)\}$ is $m$-periodic and satisfies \eqref{eq:robustAkBk}. By item (Robust2) in Lemma \ref{lem:CL-robust-Ak}, the sequence $\{B_k\}$ satisfies $m$-periodic generalized hyperbolicity with constants $C_1, \lambda_1$. In both cases denote the spaces corresponding to generalized hyperbolicity for $\{B_k\}$ by $\tilde{E}_k^s$, $\tilde{E}_k^u$. Define (slightly abusing notation) for point~$y_k$ the spaces \begin{equation} \tilde{E}_{y_k}^{s, u} := \tilde{E}_k^{s, u}. \end{equation} If $\omega$ is an $m$-periodic trajectory, then $\tilde{E}_k^{s, u} = \tilde{E}_{k+m}^{s, u}$, and hence $\tilde{E}_{y_k}^{s, u}$ is well-defined. Moreover, Definition \ref{def:CLf} does not impose any condition on the dependence of $E_y^{s, u}$ and the corresponding projections on the point $y$. Hence the splitting defined by \eqref{eq:Eg} satisfies the conditions of generalized hyperbolicity in Definition \ref{def:CLf}.
nodes.statement_short: Each g-orbit is a pseudo-orbit of f; shadow it (periodically if periodic) and transfer GH of the f-differentials to the g-differentials by sequence robustness.

nodes.name: Choice of delta (68)
nodes.statement: \|Df(x)-Df(y)\| \leq \varepsilon/2, \quad |x-y| < M\delta.
nodes.label: eq:delta1

nodes.name: Shadowing of g-orbit (70)
nodes.statement: |y_k-x_k| \leq M\delta, \quad x_{k+1} = f(x_k), \quad k \in \mathbb{Z}.
nodes.label: eq:robustykxk

nodes.name: Closeness of differentials (71)
nodes.statement: \|A_k - B_k\| \leq \|A_k - Df(y_k)\| + \|Df(y_k) - B_k\| \leq \varepsilon/2 + \delta < \varepsilon.
nodes.label: eq:robustAkBk

nodes.name: Splitting along g-orbit (72)
nodes.statement: \tilde{E}_{y_k}^{s, u} := \tilde{E}_k^{s, u}.
nodes.label: eq:Eg

nodes.name: Use of the Axiom of Choice
nodes.statement: Note that this construction uses the Axiom of Choice, and we do not know whether this dependence can be removed. For each trajectory $\omega$ of $g$, we choose a base point $y_\omega$ and a trajectory of $f$ shadowing the trajectory of $g$ through $y_\omega$. Once these choices are fixed, the construction in Lemma~\ref{lem:CL-robust-Ak} and its equivariance under shifts define the splitting consistently along the whole trajectory $\omega$. The Axiom of Choice is used to make these selections simultaneously over all trajectories of $g$; the nonuniqueness of shadowing prevents a canonical choice.
nodes.label: rem:AoC

nodes.name: Homeomorphism $\alpha$ and linear cocycle $A$
nodes.statement: Consider a homeomorphism $\alpha: \mathbb{B} \to \mathbb{B}$ and a linear cocycle $A:\mathbb{B} \to GL(\mathbb{B})$.

nodes.name: Uniform bounds on the cocycle
nodes.statement: Assume that there exists $R > 0$ such that for any $x \in \mathbb{B}$, the operator $A(x):\mathbb{B} \to \mathbb{B}$ is a bounded linear isomorphism satisfying $ \|A(x)\|, \|A^{-1}(x)\| \leq R $.

nodes.name: Uniform continuity of the cocycle
nodes.statement: Moreover, assume that $A(x)$ is uniformly continuous in $x$, i.e., for any $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $\delta > 0$ such that $$ \|A(x) - A(y)\|, \|A^{-1}(x) - A^{-1}(y)\|\leq \varepsilon, \quad \mbox{for $|x-y| < \delta$}. $$

nodes.name: Iterates $A^n_{\alpha}$ of the cocycle
nodes.statement: Denote $$ A^n_{\alpha}(x) = \begin{cases} A(\alpha^{n-1}(x))\dots A(\alpha(x))A(x), & \quad n >0,\\ Id, &\quad n = 0,\\ A^{-1}(\alpha^{n}(x)) \dots A^{-1}(\alpha^{-2}(x))A^{-1}(\alpha^{-1}(x)), & \quad n < 0. \end{cases} $$

nodes.name: Cocycle generalized hyperbolicity
nodes.statement: We say that the pair $(\alpha, A)$ satisfies \textit{cocycle generalized hyperbolicity} if there exist $C > 0$, $\lambda \in (0, 1)$ and a family of projections $P_x, Q_x: \mathbb{B} \to \mathbb{B}$ satisfying the following. \begin{itemize} \item[(C-GH1)] \textbf{Splitting.} $P_x + Q_x = Id$, $\|P_x\|, \|Q_x\| \leq C$. \\Denote $E^s_x = P_x(\mathbb{B}), E^u_x = Q_x(\mathbb{B})$; then $E^s_x \oplus E^u_x = \mathbb{B}$. \item[(C-GH2)] \textbf{Inclusion.} $A(x)E^s_x \subseteq E^s_{\alpha(x)}$, $A^{-1}(x)E^u_{\alpha(x)} \subseteq E^u_{x}$, \item[(C-GH3)] \textbf{Exponential estimates.} $$ |A^n_{\alpha}(x)v^s_x| \leq C \lambda^n |v^s_x|, \quad v^s_x \in E^s_x, n \geq 0; $$ $$ |A^{-n}_{\alpha}(x)v^u_x| \leq C \lambda^n |v^u_x|, \quad v^u_x \in E^u_x, n \geq 0. $$ \end{itemize} If, additionally, $\alpha$ and $\alpha^{-1}$ are uniformly continuous and the projections $P_x$, $Q_x$ depend uniformly continuously on $x$, i.e. satisfy \eqref{eq:cont-PQ}, then we say that $(\alpha,A)$ satisfies \textit{uniformly continuous cocycle generalized hyperbolicity}.
nodes.statement_short: A cocycle (alpha,A) is GH if bounded projections give forward-invariant E^s, backward-invariant E^u and exponential estimates; uniformly continuous if alpha^{+-1} and P_x,Q_x are.
nodes.label: def:CL-cocycle

nodes.name: Subspaces $F_x$
nodes.statement: As in Section \ref{sec:robust-Ak}, define $$ F_x := A^{-1}(x)(E_{\alpha(x)}^u) \subset E_x^u. $$

nodes.name: Space $BUC(\mathbb{B},\mathbb{B})$
nodes.statement: Let $X = BUC(\mathbb{B}, \mathbb{B})$ be the Banach space of all bounded uniformly continuous functions from $\mathbb{B}$ to itself with the supremum norm.

nodes.name: Subspace $Y$
nodes.statement: Define the subspace $Y \subset X$ by $$ Y = \{v \in X: v(x) \in E_x^s \oplus F_x\}. $$

nodes.name: Operator $T_{\alpha, A}$
nodes.statement: Define the operator $T_{\alpha, A}: X \to X$ by \begin{equation} T_{\alpha, A} v = w, \quad \mbox{where $w(\alpha(x)) = v(\alpha(x)) - A(x)v(x)$}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Cocycle difference operator (73)
nodes.statement: T_{\alpha, A} v = w, \quad \mbox{where $w(\alpha(x)) = v(\alpha(x)) - A(x)v(x)$}.
nodes.label: eq:Twv

nodes.name: Bounded inverse for cocycles
nodes.statement: Assume that $(\alpha, A)$ satisfies the uniformly continuous cocycle generalized hyperbolicity with constants~$C, \lambda$. Then there exists $L = L(\lambda, C)$, such that the restriction $T_{\alpha, A}: Y \to X$ is a bijection and admits a bounded inverse \begin{equation} S_{\alpha, A} = T^{-1}_{\alpha, A}: X \to Y, \quad \|S_{\alpha, A}\| \leq L. \end{equation}
assumptions: Assume that $(\alpha, A)$ satisfies the uniformly continuous cocycle generalized hyperbolicity with constants~$C, \lambda$.
conclusions: Then there exists $L = L(\lambda, C)$, such that the restriction $T_{\alpha, A}: Y \to X$ is a bijection and admits a bounded inverse
nodes.label: lem:SS1

nodes.name: Bounded inverse S (74)
nodes.statement: S_{\alpha, A} = T^{-1}_{\alpha, A}: X \to Y, \quad \|S_{\alpha, A}\| \leq L.
nodes.label: eq:Sf

nodes.name: Generalization of Bernardes–Messaoudi
nodes.statement: This statement generalizes \cite[Theorem 1, Step 1]{NilsonAli}, where the case in which $A(x)$ is a constant generalized hyperbolic isomorphism was considered.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma (bounded inverse for cocycles)
nodes.statement:

Given $w \in X$, define $v = S_{\alpha, A}w$ by  egin{equation} v(x) = \sum_{i \leq 0} A^{-i}_{\alpha}(\alpha^i(x)) P_{\alpha^i(x)}w(\alpha^i(x)) -\sum_{i>0}A^{-i}_{\alpha}(\alpha^i(x))Q_{\alpha^i(x)}w(\alpha^i(x)). \end{equation} As in Lemma ef{lem:SBS}, the series \eqref{eq:Svdef} converges for every $x$ and defines a function $v$ that satisfies \eqref{eq:Twv}. Define $v_n = v_n^s + v_n^u$, where $v_n^s \in E^s_{\alpha^n(x)}$, $v_n^u \in F_{\alpha^n(x)}$. nodes.name: Series for S (75)
nodes.statement: v(x) = \sum_{i \leq 0} A^{-i}_{\alpha}(\alpha^i(x)) P_{\alpha^i(x)}w(\alpha^i(x)) -\sum_{i>0}A^{-i}_{\alpha}(\alpha^i(x))Q_{\alpha^i(x)}w(\alpha^i(x)).
nodes.label: eq:Svdef

nodes.name: Kernel equation (76)
nodes.statement: T_{\alpha, A}v = 0.
nodes.label: eq:KerT

nodes.name: Uniformly continuous dependence of $H^s_x$
nodes.statement: Consider a cocycle $(\alpha, A)$ satisfying uniformly continuous cocycle generalized hyperbolicity. We say that the linear mappings $H^s_x:E^s_x \to F_x$ depend uniformly continuously on $x$ if the mappings $$ \hat{H}^s_x:\mathbb{B} \to \mathbb{B}, \quad \mbox{ with $\hat{H}^s_x(v) := H^s_x(P_x v)$} $$ are uniformly continuous in $x$ in the operator norm. Similarly, we define the uniform continuity for $H^u_{x}: E_{\alpha(x)}^u \to A(x)E_x^s \subset E_{\alpha(x)}^s$.

nodes.name: Robustness of cocycle generalized hyperbolicity under base perturbation
nodes.statement: Assume that the pair $(\alpha, A)$ satisfies uniformly continuous cocycle generalized hyperbolicity with constants $C > 0$, $\lambda \in (0, 1)$. Then for any $\lambda_1 \in (\lambda, 1)$ and $\varepsilon >0$ there exist $C_1 > 1$ and $\delta >0$ such that for any homeomorphism $\beta: \mathbb{B} \to \mathbb{B}$, with $\beta$ and $\beta^{-1}$ uniformly continuous, satisfying \begin{equation} |\alpha(x) - \beta(x)|, |\alpha^{-1}(x) - \beta^{-1}(x)| < \delta, \quad x \in \mathbb{B} \end{equation} there exist mappings $H^s_x: E_x^s \to F_x \subset E_x^u$, $H^u_{x}: E_{\alpha(x)}^u \to A(x)E_x^s \subset E_{\alpha(x)}^s$ that depend uniformly continuously on $x$ such that $ \|H^s_x\|, \|H^u_x\| < \varepsilon $ and the pair $(\beta, A)$ satisfies uniformly continuous cocycle generalized hyperbolicity with constants $(C_1, \lambda_1)$ and spaces \begin{align*} \tilde{E}_x^s &= (Id + H^s_x)E^s_x = \{v+H^s_x v: v \in E^s_x\},\\ \tilde{E}_{\beta(x)}^u &= (Id + H^u_x)E^u_{\alpha(x)} = \{v+H^u_x v: v \in E^u_{\alpha(x)}\}. \end{align*} There exists $\varepsilon_0$ such that if $\varepsilon < \varepsilon_0$ then \begin{equation} \tilde{E}^s_x \oplus A^{-1}(x)\tilde{E}^u_{\beta(x)} = E^s_x \oplus F_x. \end{equation}
assumptions: Assume that the pair $(\alpha, A)$ satisfies uniformly continuous cocycle generalized hyperbolicity with constants $C > 0$, $\lambda \in (0, 1)$.
conclusions: the pair $(\beta, A)$ satisfies uniformly continuous cocycle generalized hyperbolicity with constants $(C_1, \lambda_1)$ and spaces
There exists $\varepsilon_0$ such that if $\varepsilon < \varepsilon_0$ then
nodes.statement_short: Perturbing the base map alpha to a nearby beta keeps cocycle GH, with graph-transformed spaces, and preserves E^s + F.
nodes.label: lem:SS2

nodes.name: Closeness of base maps (77)
nodes.statement: |\alpha(x) - \beta(x)|, |\alpha^{-1}(x) - \beta^{-1}(x)| < \delta, \quad x \in \mathbb{B}
nodes.label: eq:al-be-ep

nodes.name: Preservation of E^s + F (78)
nodes.statement: \tilde{E}^s_x \oplus A^{-1}(x)\tilde{E}^u_{\beta(x)} = E^s_x \oplus F_x.
nodes.label: eq:tildeE-EF

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma (cocycle robustness)
nodes.statement_short: Graph transform as for sequences: block estimates (B1),(B2), then contraction fixed points for H^s and H^u in uniformly continuous operator families. A separate argument proves the sum E^s+F is unchanged.

nodes.name: Closeness of blocks (80)
nodes.statement: \|A_x^{ss} - B_x^{ss}\|, \|A_x^{us} - B_x^{us}\|,\|A_x^{su} - B_x^{su}\|,\|A_x^{uu} - B_x^{uu}\| < \varepsilon_1, \quad x \in \mathbb{B}.
nodes.label: eq:AB-ep1

nodes.name: Right inverse Z_x (81)
nodes.statement: B^{uu}_{x} Z_x = Id|_{E_{\beta(x)}^u}, \|Z_x\| \leq (1+\varepsilon_1)R,
nodes.label: eq:Zx-cond

nodes.name: Exponential estimate for Z (82)
nodes.statement: \|Z_{\beta^{-n}(x)} \dots Z_{\beta^{-2}(x)}Z_{\beta^{-1}(x)}\| \leq C_2\lambda_2^n, \quad n \geq 0, x \in \mathbb{B}.
nodes.label: eq:Zx-exp

nodes.name: Invariance condition for H^s (83)
nodes.statement: A(x)(v^s+ H^s_xv^s) = w^s+ H^s_{\beta(x)}(w^s)
nodes.label: eq:Hsx-cond1

nodes.name: Equation for H^s via B (84)
nodes.statement: B^{uu}_x H^s_x = H_{\beta(x)}^s(B^{ss}_x + B^{su}_xH^s_x) - B^{us}_x.
nodes.label: eq:H-via-B

nodes.name: Fixed-point equation for H^s (85)
nodes.statement: H_x^s = Z_x H^s_{\beta(x)} B_x^{ss} + (Z_x H^s_{\beta(x)}B^{su}_xH^s_x - Z_xB^{us}_x).
nodes.label: eq:H-via-Z

nodes.name: Norm bound for F (cocycle) (86)

nodes.name: Equation for H^u (88)

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem (structural stability)
nodes.statement: Assume that $f$ satisfies uniformly continuous generalized hyperbolicity with constants $C > 0$, $\lambda \in (0, 1)$. Then the pair $(f, Df)$ satisfies uniformly continuous cocycle generalized hyperbolicity. Let $\varepsilon_0$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:SS2}. Choose $\varepsilon_1 \in (0,\varepsilon_0)$ and $\lambda_1\in(\lambda,1)$, and let $C_1>1$ and $\delta>0$ be the corresponding constants. Let $R > 1$ be the constant in \eqref{eq:C1-2}, $L = L(C_1, \lambda_1)>0$ be the constant provided by Lemma \ref{lem:SS1}. Set $\varepsilon=\frac{1}{3L}$. Choose $d_0 < \min(\frac{\delta}{R}, \frac{1}{3L})$, such that \eqref{eq:s-Lip} holds with this $\varepsilon$ for $|v_1|, |v_2| < 2Ld_0$. Fix $d\in(0,d_0)$ and $g\in\mathfrak{D}(\mathbb{B})$ satisfying $\|g-f\|_{C^1}<d$. Denote $\Delta = g - f$. Then \begin{equation} |\Delta(x)| < d, \quad \|D\Delta(x)\| < d, \quad x \in \mathbb{B}. \end{equation} Moreover, for every $x\in\mathbb{B}$, setting $y=g^{-1}(x)$, we have \[ |f^{-1}(x)-g^{-1}(x)| = |f^{-1}(g(y))-f^{-1}(f(y))| \leq R|g(y)-f(y)| <Rd<\delta. \] Together with $\sup_x|f(x)-g(x)|<d<\delta$, this verifies \eqref{eq:al-be-ep}. By Lemma \ref{lem:SS2}, the pair $(g, Df)$ satisfies uniformly continuous cocycle generalized hyperbolicity with constants~$C_1, \lambda_1$. Denote the splitting corresponding to the pair $(f, Df)$ by $$ \mathbb{B} = E^s_x \oplus E^u_x, \quad F_x = (Df(x))^{-1}E^u_{f(x)} \subset E^u_x $$ and splitting provided by Lemma \ref{lem:SS2} corresponding to pair $(g, Df)$ by \begin{equation}\notag \mathbb{B} = \tilde{E}^s_x \oplus \tilde{E}^u_x, \quad \tilde{F}_x = (Df(x))^{-1}\tilde{E}^u_{g(x)} \subset \tilde{E}^u_x. \end{equation} \begin{remark} We do not claim that the pair $(g, Dg)$ satisfies uniformly continuous cocycle generalized hyperbolicity, although we believe it to be true. \end{remark} According to \eqref{eq:tildeE-EF} the following equality holds $ \tilde{E}^s_x \oplus \tilde{F}_x = {E}^s_x \oplus {F}_x. $ Hence $$ \{v \in X: v(x) \in \tilde{E}_x^s \oplus \tilde{F}_x\} = Y. $$ By Lemma \ref{lem:SS1} there exist operators $O_f, O_g: X \to Y$ satisfying $$ T_{f, Df}O_f = Id_X, \; \|O_f\| \leq L, \quad T_{g, Df}O_g = Id_X, \; \|O_g\| \leq L. $$ Denote $M = 2L$. \textbf{Step 1.} First, we find a map $h_1: \mathbb{B} \to \mathbb{B}$, $h_1 \in Y$, satisfying \eqref{eq:conj-h1}. Substituting $g = f + \Delta$ in equation \eqref{eq:conj-h1} and using the definition of $s_f$ we get $$ f(x) + Df(x)h_1(x) + s_f(x, h_1(x)) + \Delta(x+h_1(x)) = f(x) + h_1(f(x)), \quad x \in \mathbb{B}. $$ Canceling $f(x)$ and regrouping terms we get \begin{equation} h_1(f(x)) = Df(x)h_1(x) + s_f(x, h_1(x)) + \Delta(x+h_1(x)), \quad x \in \mathbb{B}. \end{equation} In order for \eqref{eq:conj-final} to hold, it suffices that \begin{equation} h_1(x) = O_f(s_f(x, h_1(x)) + \Delta(x+h_1(x))). \end{equation} Consider the (nonlinear) operator $G_f:BUC(\mathbb{B}, \mathbb{B}) \to BUC(\mathbb{B}, \mathbb{B})$ defined by $$ G_f(h_1)(x) = s_f(x, h_1(x)) + \Delta(x+h_1(x)), \quad x \in \mathbb{B}. $$ Using \eqref{eq:s-Lip} and \eqref{eq:Delta-c1} we conclude that for $|h_1|, |h'_1| \leq 2L d$ the following inequalities hold \begin{multline*} |(G_f(h_1)-G_f(h'_1))(x)| = |s_f(x, h_1(x)) - s_f(x, h'_1(x)) + \Delta(x+h_1(x)) - \Delta(x+h'_1(x))| \leq \\ (\varepsilon+d)|h_1(x) - h'_1(x)| \leq \frac{2}{3L}\|h_1 - h'_1\|. \end{multline*} Using \eqref{eq:Sf} we conclude that $ \|O_f \circ G_f(h_1) - O_f \circ G_f(h'_1)\| \leq \frac{2}{3}\|h_1-h'_1\|, $ hence $O_f \circ G_f$ is a contraction. For $\|h_1\| \leq 2Ld$, equations \eqref{eq:s-Lip}, \eqref{eq:Delta-c1} imply $\|G_f(h_1)\| \leq \varepsilon 2Ld + d$, and $$ \|O_f \circ G_f(h_1)\| \leq L(\varepsilon \cdot 2Ld + d) = \left(\frac{2L}{3}+L\right)d \leq 2Ld. $$ The latter implies existence and uniqueness of a map $h_1$ with $\|h_1\| \leq 2Ld$ satisfying $O_f \circ G_f (h_1) = h_1$, and hence \eqref{eq:conj-h1}. Therefore $h_1$ satisfies \eqref{eq:h1h2leqMdelta}. Note that $\mbox{Im }O_f = Y$ and hence $h_1 \in Y$. \textbf{Step 2.} To construct a map $h_2 \in Y$, satisfying \eqref{eq:conj-h2} we follow an approach similar to that of Step 1. For completeness, we provide the full proof below. The conjugacy \eqref{eq:conj-h2} is equivalent to $$ f(x+h_2(x)) = f(x) + \Delta(x) + h_2(g(x)), \quad x \in \mathbb{B}. $$ Using definition of $s_f$ and canceling $f(x)$ we get \begin{equation} h_2(g(x)) = Df(x)h_2(x) + s_f(x, h_2(x)) + \Delta(x), \quad x \in \mathbb{B}. \end{equation} In order for \eqref{eq:conj-final-g} to hold, it suffices that \begin{equation} h_2(x) = O_g(s_f(x, h_2(x)) + \Delta(x)). \end{equation} Consider the (nonlinear) operator $G_g:BUC(\mathbb{B}, \mathbb{B}) \to BUC(\mathbb{B}, \mathbb{B})$ defined by $$ G_g(h_2)(x) = s_f(x, h_2(x)) + \Delta(x), \quad x \in \mathbb{B}. $$ Using \eqref{eq:s-Lip} and \eqref{eq:Delta-c1} we conclude that for $|h_2|, |h'_2| \leq 2L d$ the following inequalities hold \begin{multline*} |(G_g(h_2)-G_g(h'_2))(x)| = |s_f(x, h_2(x)) - s_f(x, h'_2(x))| \leq \varepsilon|h_2(x) - h'_2(x)| \leq \frac{1}{3L}\|h_2 - h'_2\|. \end{multline*} Using \eqref{eq:Sf} we conclude that $ \|O_g \circ G_g(h_2) - O_g \circ G_g(h'_2)\| \leq \frac{1}{3}\|h_2-h'_2\| $ and hence $O_g \circ G_g$ is a contraction. If $\|h_2\| \leq 2Ld$ then \eqref{eq:s-Lip} and \eqref{eq:Delta-c1} imply $\|G_g(h_2)\| \leq \varepsilon 2Ld + d$, and $$ \|O_g \circ G_g(h_2)\| \leq L(\varepsilon \cdot 2Ld + d) = \left(\frac{2L}{3}+L\right)d \leq 2Ld. $$ The latter implies existence and uniqueness of a map $h_2$ with $\|h_2\| \leq 2Ld$ satisfying $ O_g \circ G_g (h_2) = h_2, $ and hence \eqref{eq:conj-final-g}. Therefore, $h_2$ satisfies \eqref{eq:conj-h2} and \eqref{eq:h1h2leqMdelta}. Note that $\mbox{Im }O_g = Y$, hence $h_2 \in Y$. This proves Theorem~\ref{thm:SS}\,(\ref{item:SS-semi}). \textbf{Step 3.} Under the additional assumption in Theorem~\ref{thm:SS}\,(\ref{item:SS-full}), we prove \eqref{eq:Idh-homeo}. From \eqref{eq:conj-h1} and \eqref{eq:conj-h2} we obtain the following. \begin{equation} f \circ (Id+h_2) \circ (Id+h_1) = (Id+h_2) \circ (Id+h_1) \circ f, \end{equation} \begin{equation} g \circ (Id+h_1) \circ (Id+h_2) = (Id+h_1) \circ (Id+h_2) \circ g. \end{equation} Since $h_1, h_2 \in Y$ and the spaces $E^s_x \oplus (Df(x))^{-1}E^u_{f(x)} = E^s_x \oplus F_x$ do not depend on $x$, for some functions $h_3, h_4 \in Y$ the following hold $$ (Id+h_2) \circ (Id+h_1) = Id + h_3, \quad (Id+h_1) \circ (Id+h_2) = Id + h_4. $$ \begin{equation} h_3(x), h_4(x) \in E^s_x \oplus F_x, \quad |h_3(x)|, |h_4(x)| \leq 2Md, \quad x \in \mathbb{B}. \end{equation} By \eqref{eq:selff} the identity $ f\circ (Id+h_3) = (Id+h_3) \circ f $ holds. Arguing as in Step~1, we conclude that $$ h_3(f(x)) - Df(x)h_3(x) = s_f(x, h_3(x)). $$ Since $h_3 \in Y$, Lemma \ref{lem:SS1} implies that \begin{equation} h_3 = O_f(s_f(x, h_3(x))). \end{equation} Similarly to the operator $O_f \circ G_f$, the map $h_3 \to O_f(s_f(x, h_3(x)))$ is a contraction (decreasing $d$ if necessary) on the set of $h_3$ with $\|h_3\| \leq 2Md$. Therefore, equation \eqref{eq:h3-fixed} has a unique solution for $h_3$ satisfying \eqref{eq:h3h4-cond}. On the other hand, $h_3 \equiv 0$ satisfies both \eqref{eq:h3h4-cond} and \eqref{eq:h3-fixed}. By uniqueness $h_3 \equiv 0$. The argument for $h_4$ is analogous. Equation \eqref{eq:selfg} implies that $g \circ (Id+h_4) = (Id+h_4) \circ g$. Arguing as in Step~2, we obtain $$ h_4(g(x)) - Df(x)h_4(x) = s_f(x, h_4(x)) + \left( \Delta(x+h_4(x)) - \Delta(x) \right). $$ As in the proof for $h_3$, this equation has a unique solution $h_4$, satisfying \eqref{eq:h3h4-cond}. Hence, $h_4 \equiv 0$. This completes the proof of \eqref{eq:Idh-homeo} and Theorem \ref{thm:SS}\,(\ref{item:SS-full}).
nodes.statement_short: Apply cocycle results to (f,Df) and (g,Df); find h_1, h_2 in Y as contraction fixed points. If E^s+F is constant, uniqueness forces the compositions to be the identity.

This required special attention in Lemma \ref{lem:SS2} to establish equality \eqref{eq:tildeE-EF}. Let $ X=C_b(\mathbb{B},\mathbb{B}) $ be the Banach space of bounded continuous functions with the supremum norm, and let $T_{\alpha,A}:X\to X$ be defined by \eqref{eq:Twv}. Then there exist a constant $L=L(\lambda,C)$ and a not necessarily linear map $S_{\alpha,A}:X\to X$ such that $ T_{\alpha,A}\circ S_{\alpha,A}=Id_X, $ and $S_{\alpha,A}$ is Lipschitz with constant $L$.

nodes.name: Does Lipschitz shadowing imply generalized hyperbolicity in Banach spaces?
nodes.statement: On compact finite-dimensional manifolds, Lipschitz shadowing implies generalized hyperbolicity by \cite{TikhLipSh} and Theorem~\ref{stat:finite-dimensional-characterization}. We ask whether the same implication holds in Banach spaces.

nodes.name: Does the bounded solution property imply generalized hyperbolicity?
nodes.statement: The main difficulty is the converse linear implication: whether the bounded solution property implies generalized hyperbolicity.

nodes.name: Equivalence of bounded and strong bounded solution properties
nodes.statement: In general Banach spaces there is an additional difficulty: it is not known whether the bounded and strong bounded solution properties are equivalent.

nodes.name: Error-halving for linear operators
nodes.statement: Assume that $T$ has the finite Lipschitz shadowing property with constant $L$. Then for every $d>0$ and every $d$-pseudotrajectory $\{x_j\}_{j \in \mathbb{Z}}$ of $T$ there exists a $\tfrac{d}{2}$-pseudotrajectory $\{x'_j\}_{j \in \mathbb{Z}}$ of $T$ such that $$ \|x_j - x'_j\| \le Ld, \qquad j \in \mathbb{Z}. $$
assumptions: Assume that $T$ has the finite Lipschitz shadowing property with constant $L$.
conclusions: Then for every $d>0$ and every $d$-pseudotrajectory $\{x_j\}_{j \in \mathbb{Z}}$ of $T$ there exists a $\tfrac{d}{2}$-pseudotrajectory $\{x'_j\}_{j \in \mathbb{Z}}$ of $T$ such that
nodes.label: lem:halving

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma (error halving for operators)
nodes.statement: Fix an integer $m \ge 4L$ and set $ n_k := \frac{k(k-1)}{2}m $, so that $n_0 = n_1 = 0$ and $n_{k+1} - n_k = km$ for $k \ge 1$; the intervals $[n_k, n_{k+1})$, $k \ge 1$, partition $[0, +\infty) \cap \mathbb{Z}$. For each $k \ge 1$ the restriction $\{x_j\}_{|j| \le n_{k+1}}$ is a finite $d$-pseudotrajectory, so by the finite Lipschitz shadowing property there is $u_k \in X$ with \begin{equation} \|x_j - T^j u_k\| \le Ld \qquad (|j| \le n_{k+1}). \end{equation} We interpolate linearly between consecutive shadowing points. For $j \ge 0$ write $j = n_k + i$ with $k \ge 1$ and $0 \le i < km$, and put $$ x'_j := \Big(1 - \tfrac{i}{km}\Big) T^j u_k + \tfrac{i}{km}\, T^j u_{k+1}; $$ for $j < 0$ write $-j = n_k + i$ in the same way and put $x'_j := \big(1 - \tfrac{i}{km}\big) T^j u_k + \tfrac{i}{km}\, T^j u_{k+1}$. \textbf{Displacement.} Let $j \ge 0$, $j = n_k + i$. Then $j \le n_{k+1} \le n_{k+2}$, so \eqref{eq:BP-uk} holds at $j$ both for $u_k$ and for $u_{k+1}$; as $x'_j$ is a convex combination of $T^j u_k$ and $T^j u_{k+1}$, $$ \|x_j - x'_j\| \le \Big(1-\tfrac{i}{km}\Big)\|x_j - T^j u_k\| + \tfrac{i}{km}\,\|x_j - T^j u_{k+1}\| \le Ld. $$ The case $j<0$ is identical, so $\|x_j - x'_j\| \le Ld$ for all $j \in \mathbb{Z}$. \textbf{Halved error.} Let $j \ge 0$, $j = n_k + i$ with $0 \le i < km$. If $i+1 \le km-1$, then $j+1$ lies in the same block and a direct computation gives $$ Tx'_j - x'_{j+1} = \tfrac{1}{km}\big(T^{j+1}u_k - T^{j+1}u_{k+1}\big). $$ If $i+1 = km$, then $j+1 = n_{k+1}$ is the first index of the next block, where $x'_{j+1} = T^{j+1}u_{k+1}$, and the same identity follows since $x'_j = \tfrac{1}{km}T^{j}u_k + \big(1-\tfrac{1}{km}\big)T^{j}u_{k+1}$ in this case. In either case $j+1 \le n_{k+1} \le n_{k+2}$, so \eqref{eq:BP-uk} applies at $j+1$ for both $u_k$ and $u_{k+1}$, and therefore $$ \|Tx'_j - x'_{j+1}\| \le \tfrac{1}{km}\Big(\|T^{j+1}u_k - x_{j+1}\| + \|x_{j+1} - T^{j+1}u_{k+1}\|\Big) \le \frac{2Ld}{km} \le \frac{2Ld}{m} \le \frac{d}{2}, $$ where we used $k \ge 1$ and $m \ge 4L$. The estimate for $j < 0$, including the junction between $j=-1$ and $j=0$, is analogous. Hence, $\{x'_j\}$ is a $\tfrac{d}{2}$-pseudotrajectory.
nodes.statement_short: Interpolate linearly between finite shadowing points on blocks of growing length km; displacement stays Ld and the one-step error is at most d/2.

nodes.name: Finite shadowing points u_k (100)
nodes.statement: \|x_j - T^j u_k\| \le Ld \qquad (|j| \le n_{k+1}).
nodes.label: eq:BP-uk

nodes.name: Proof of the Bernardes–Peris theorem with constant $2L$
nodes.statement: Let $\{x_j\}_{j \in \mathbb{Z}}$ be a $d$-pseudotrajectory of $T$. Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:halving} repeatedly, we construct pseudotrajectories $\{x^{(l)}_j\}_{j \in \mathbb{Z}}$, $l \ge 0$, with $x^{(0)}_j = x_j$ and, for every $l \ge 0$, $$ \{x^{(l+1)}_j\}\ \text{is a}\ \tfrac{d}{2^{l+1}}\text{-pseudotrajectory}, \qquad \|x^{(l+1)}_j - x^{(l)}_j\| \le L\,\frac{d}{2^{l}} \quad (j \in \mathbb{Z}), $$ where the displacement bound uses that $\{x^{(l)}_j\}$ is a $\tfrac{d}{2^{l}}$-pseudotrajectory. Fix $j \in \mathbb{Z}$. The bound $\|x^{(l+1)}_j - x^{(l)}_j\| \le Ld\,2^{-l}$ shows that $\big(x^{(l)}_j\big)_{l \ge 0}$ is a Cauchy sequence in $X$; let $v_j := \lim_{l \to \infty} x^{(l)}_j$. Letting $l \to \infty$ in $\|Tx^{(l)}_j - x^{(l)}_{j+1}\| \le d\,2^{-l}$ yields $Tv_j = v_{j+1}$, so $\{v_j\}$ is an exact trajectory, that is, $v_j = T^j v$ with $v := v_0$. Finally, $$ \|x_j - T^j v\| = \|x^{(0)}_j - v_j\| \le \sum_{l \ge 0} \|x^{(l)}_j - x^{(l+1)}_j\| \le \sum_{l \ge 0} L\,\frac{d}{2^{l}} = 2Ld. $$ As $j \in \mathbb{Z}$ was arbitrary, $T$ has the Lipschitz shadowing property with constant $2L$.
nodes.statement_short: Iterate the error-halving lemma; the corrections are summable and converge to an exact trajectory within 2Ld.

nodes.name: Compact manifold $M$ and diffeomorphism $f$
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional smooth compact manifold equipped with a Riemannian metric, and let $f:M\to M$ be a $C^1$-diffeomorphism.

nodes.name: Generalized hyperbolicity on manifolds
nodes.statement: We say that $f$ satisfies generalized hyperbolicity if the tangent-bundle analogue of Definition~\ref{def:CLf} holds: there exist $C>0$, $\lambda\in(0,1)$ and projections \[ P_x,Q_x:T_xM\to T_xM, \qquad E_x^s=P_x(T_xM),\quad E_x^u=Q_x(T_xM), \] satisfying conditions {\rm(GH1)}--{\rm(GH3)}, with $\mathbb{B}$ replaced by $T_xM$.

nodes.name: Sets $B^+(p)$ and $B^-(p)$
nodes.statement: For $p\in M$, define \[ B^+(p)= \left\{ v\in T_pM: |Df^n(p)v|\to0\ \text{as }n\to+\infty \right\}, \] \[ B^-(p)= \left\{ v\in T_pM: |Df^n(p)v|\to0\ \text{as }n\to-\infty \right\}. \]

nodes.name: Mañé's infinitesimal criterion
nodes.statement: A $C^1$-diffeomorphism $f:M\to M$ is structurally stable if and only if \begin{equation} B^+(p)+B^-(p)=T_pM \qquad\text{for every }p\in M. \end{equation}
assumptions: A $C^1$-diffeomorphism $f:M\to M$

nodes.name: Mañé's transversality condition (101)
nodes.statement: B^+(p)+B^-(p)=T_pM \qquad\text{for every }p\in M.

nodes.name: Justification of the uniform orbitwise structure
nodes.statement:
The constants in this statement are independent of the trajectory. We recall the ingredients of the Robbin--Robinson construction responsible for this uniformity. 
oindent	extbf{Adapted metric.} Let $|\cdot|_0$ denote the norm of the Riemannian metric fixed above. Since $\Omega(f)$ is hyperbolic, the standard adapted-metric construction gives a continuous Riemannian norm $|\cdot|_*$ and a number $	heta_0\in(0,1)$ such that \[ |Df(x)v^s|_*\leq	heta_0|v^s|_*, \qquad |D(f^{-1})(x)v^u|_*\leq	heta_0|v^u|_* \] for $x\in\Omega(f)$, $v^s\in E_{\Omega,x}^s$, and $v^u\in E_{\Omega,x}^u$. Extend this metric to $M$. Robinson's compatible-bundle construction then provides neighborhoods of the basic sets and a number $	heta\in(	heta_0,1)$ for which the one-step estimates in Proposition~ef{stat:Robinson-bundles} hold. This is the adapted metric used in Robinson's construction; see the proof of Theorem~5.1 in \cite{Robinson1976}. Since $M$ is compact, the two norms are uniformly equivalent: there is $\kappa\geq1$ such that  egin{equation} \kappa^{-1}|v|_0\leq|v|_*\leq\kappa|v|_0, \qquad v\in TM. \end{equation} 
oindent	extbf{Compatible bundles.} Let $ \Omega(f)=\Omega_1\cup\cdots\cup\Omega_m $ be the spectral decomposition. In the notation of this paper, Proposition~7.1 of \cite[p.~66]{Robinson1976} gives the following statement with respect to the adapted metric.  egin{statement}[Robinson, Proposition~7.1] There exist neighborhoods $Z_i$ of $\Omega_i$, continuous subbundles $E_i^u,E_i^s$ of $TM|_{\mathcal O(Z_i)}$, $i=1,\ldots,m$, and $	heta\in(0,1)$ such that:  egin{itemize} \item[(1)] $E_i^u$ and $E_i^s$ are invariant under $Df$; \item[(2)] if $x\in\mathcal O^+(Z_j)\cap\mathcal O^-(Z_i)$, then $ E_{i,x}^u\subseteq E_{j,x}^u$, $E_{i,x}^s\supseteq E_{j,x}^s; $ \item[(3)] $ E_{i,x}^u \oplus E_{i,x}^s=T_xM$, for any $x\in\mathcal O(Z_i) $; \item[(4)] if $x\in Z_i$, $v^s\in E_{i,x}^s$, and $v^u\in E_{i,x}^u$, then $$ |Df(x)v^s|_*\leq	heta|v^s|_*, \qquad |D(f^{-1})(x)v^u|_*\leq	heta|v^u|_*. $$ \end{itemize} Here $ \mathcal O^+(Z)= igcup_{n\geq0}f^n(Z)$, $\mathcal O^-(Z)= igcup_{n\leq0}f^n(Z)$, $\mathcal O(Z)=\mathcal O^+(Z)\cup\mathcal O^-(Z) $. The one-step estimates in item~(4) are asserted for $x\in Z_i$, not for all $x\in\mathcal O(Z_i)$. \end{statement} The following uniform consequences are stated immediately after the proof of Proposition~7.1 in \cite[p.~66]{Robinson1976}. We label them (5) and (6) for use below; they are unnumbered in Robinson's paper.  egin{statement}[Uniform estimates following Proposition~7.1] Let $\{\gamma_i\}_{i=1}^m$ be a $C^{\infty}$ partition of unity subordinate to the finite open cover $\{\mathcal O(Z_i)\}_{i=1}^m$. There exists an integer $q\geq0$ such that, for every $i$ and every $x\in\mathrm{supp}\gamma_i$,  egin{itemize} \item the forward orbit of $x$ lies in $ igcup_{j\geq i}Z_j$ except at most $q$ iterates; \item the backward orbit of $x$ lies in $ igcup_{j\leq i}Z_j$ except at most $q$ iterates. \end{itemize} Set $ b_*:=\sup_{x\in M}\max\left\{\|Df(x)\|_*,\|D(f^{-1})(x)\|_*ight\}$, $C_*:= rac{b_*^q}{	heta^q}. $ Then:  egin{itemize} \item[(5)] for every $x\in\mathrm{supp}\gamma_i$, $n\geq0$, $v^s\in E_{i,x}^s$, and $v^u\in E_{i,x}^u$,  egin{equation} |Df^n(x)v^s|_*\leq C_*	heta^n|v^s|_*, \qquad |D(f^{-n})(x)v^u|_*\leq C_*	heta^n|v^u|_*; \end{equation} \item[(6)] the stable and unstable bundles are uniformly transverse on $\operatorname{supp}\gamma_i$. Consequently, there exists $C_{\mathrm{proj},*}>0$, independent of $i$ and $x$, such that the projections \[ \pi_{i,x}^s:T_xM	o E_{i,x}^s \quad	ext{along }E_{i,x}^u, \qquad \pi_{i,x}^u:T_xM	o E_{i,x}^u \quad	ext{along }E_{i,x}^s \] satisfy $ \|\pi_{i,x}^s\|_*, \|\pi_{i,x}^u\|_* \leq C_{\mathrm{proj},*}$, for $x\in\operatorname{supp}\gamma_i. $ \end{itemize} \end{statement} Indeed, compatibility allows item~(4) of Proposition~ef{stat:Robinson-bundles} to be applied at every nonexceptional iterate. At each of the at most $q$ exceptional iterates, the norm increases by at most $b_*$. Hence $ b_*^q	heta^{n-q}=C_*	heta^n, $ which gives item~(5). Item~(6) follows from continuity of the bundles, compactness of $\mathrm{supp}\gamma_i$, and finiteness of the family. 
oindent	extbf{Return to the original metric.} By \eqref{eq:app-equivalent-metrics}, items~(5)--(6) remain valid in the original metric after replacing their constants by $ C_1:=\kappa^2\max\{C_*,C_{\mathrm{proj},*}\}. $ Thus, for $x\in\mathrm{supp}\gamma_i$, $n\geq0$, $v^s\in E_{i,x}^s$, and $v^u\in E_{i,x}^u$,  egin{equation} |Df^n(x)v^s|_0\leq C_1	heta^n|v^s|_0, \quad |D(f^{-n})(x)v^u|_0\leq C_1	heta^n|v^u|_0, \quad \|\pi_{i,x}^s\|_0,\|\pi_{i,x}^u\|_0\leq C_1. \end{equation} Consequently, all constants in the compatible-bundle construction are uniform in the original metric. Together with the orbitwise gluing in the Robbin--Robinson construction, this yields Proposition~ef{stat:uniform-CL-finite}; see also \cite[p.~277, after Definition~3]{PilCL}.
nodes.statement_short: Recall Robinson's adapted metric and compatible bundles with uniform estimates, then return to the original metric with constant kappa^2.

nodes.name: Equivalence of metrics (102)
nodes.statement: \kappa^{-1}|v|_0\leq|v|_*\leq\kappa|v|_0, \qquad v\in TM.
nodes.label: eq:app-equivalent-metrics

nodes.name: Robinson's compatible bundles (Proposition 7.1)
nodes.statement: There exist neighborhoods $Z_i$ of $\Omega_i$, continuous subbundles $E_i^u,E_i^s$ of $TM|_{\mathcal O(Z_i)}$, $i=1,\ldots,m$, and $\theta\in(0,1)$ such that: \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] $E_i^u$ and $E_i^s$ are invariant under $Df$; \item[(2)] if $x\in\mathcal O^+(Z_j)\cap\mathcal O^-(Z_i)$, then $ E_{i,x}^u\subseteq E_{j,x}^u$, $E_{i,x}^s\supseteq E_{j,x}^s; $ \item[(3)] $ E_{i,x}^u \oplus E_{i,x}^s=T_xM$, for any $x\in\mathcal O(Z_i) $; \item[(4)] if $x\in Z_i$, $v^s\in E_{i,x}^s$, and $v^u\in E_{i,x}^u$, then $$ |Df(x)v^s|_*\leq\theta|v^s|_*, \qquad |D(f^{-1})(x)v^u|_*\leq\theta|v^u|_*. $$ \end{itemize} Here $ \mathcal O^+(Z)=\bigcup_{n\geq0}f^n(Z)$, $\mathcal O^-(Z)=\bigcup_{n\leq0}f^n(Z)$, $\mathcal O(Z)=\mathcal O^+(Z)\cup\mathcal O^-(Z) $. The one-step estimates in item~(4) are asserted for $x\in Z_i$, not for all $x\in\mathcal O(Z_i)$.
conclusions: There exist neighborhoods $Z_i$ of $\Omega_i$, continuous subbundles $E_i^u,E_i^s$ of $TM|_{\mathcal O(Z_i)}$, $i=1,\ldots,m$, and $\theta\in(0,1)$ such that:
nodes.label: stat:Robinson-bundles

nodes.name: Uniform estimates following Robinson's Proposition 7.1
nodes.statement: Let $\{\gamma_i\}_{i=1}^m$ be a $C^{\infty}$ partition of unity subordinate to the finite open cover $\{\mathcal O(Z_i)\}_{i=1}^m$. There exists an integer $q\geq0$ such that, for every $i$ and every $x\in\mathrm{supp}\gamma_i$, \begin{itemize} \item the forward orbit of $x$ lies in $\bigcup_{j\geq i}Z_j$ except at most $q$ iterates; \item the backward orbit of $x$ lies in $\bigcup_{j\leq i}Z_j$ except at most $q$ iterates. \end{itemize} Set $ b_*:=\sup_{x\in M}\max\left\{\|Df(x)\|_*,\|D(f^{-1})(x)\|_*\right\}$, $C_*:=\frac{b_*^q}{\theta^q}. $ Then: \begin{itemize} \item[(5)] for every $x\in\mathrm{supp}\gamma_i$, $n\geq0$, $v^s\in E_{i,x}^s$, and $v^u\in E_{i,x}^u$, \begin{equation} |Df^n(x)v^s|_*\leq C_*\theta^n|v^s|_*, \qquad |D(f^{-n})(x)v^u|_*\leq C_*\theta^n|v^u|_*; \end{equation} \item[(6)] the stable and unstable bundles are uniformly transverse on $\operatorname{supp}\gamma_i$. Consequently, there exists $C_{\mathrm{proj},*}>0$, independent of $i$ and $x$, such that the projections \[ \pi_{i,x}^s:T_xM\to E_{i,x}^s \quad\text{along }E_{i,x}^u, \qquad \pi_{i,x}^u:T_xM\to E_{i,x}^u \quad\text{along }E_{i,x}^s \] satisfy $ \|\pi_{i,x}^s\|_*, \|\pi_{i,x}^u\|_* \leq C_{\mathrm{proj},*}$, for $x\in\operatorname{supp}\gamma_i. $ \end{itemize}
assumptions: Let $\{\gamma_i\}_{i=1}^m$ be a $C^{\infty}$ partition of unity subordinate to the finite open cover $\{\mathcal O(Z_i)\}_{i=1}^m$.
conclusions: There exists an integer $q\geq0$ such that, for every $i$ and every $x\in\mathrm{supp}\gamma_i$,
nodes.label: stat:Robinson-uniform

nodes.name: Uniform estimates in adapted metric (103)
nodes.statement: |Df^n(x)v^s|_*\leq C_*\theta^n|v^s|_*, \qquad |D(f^{-n})(x)v^u|_*\leq C_*\theta^n|v^u|_*;
nodes.label: eq:app-Robinson-stable

nodes.name: Justification of the uniform estimates (5)-(6)
nodes.statement: Indeed, compatibility allows item~(4) of Proposition~\ref{stat:Robinson-bundles} to be applied at every nonexceptional iterate. At each of the at most $q$ exceptional iterates, the norm increases by at most $b_*$. Hence $ b_*^q\theta^{n-q}=C_*\theta^n, $ which gives item~(5). Item~(6) follows from continuity of the bundles, compactness of $\mathrm{supp}\gamma_i$, and finiteness of the family.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the one-step contraction at non-exceptional iterates and pay b_* at the at most q exceptional ones; transversality by compactness.

nodes.name: Uniform estimates in original metric (104)
nodes.statement: |Df^n(x)v^s|_0\leq C_1\theta^n|v^s|_0, \quad |D(f^{-n})(x)v^u|_0\leq C_1\theta^n|v^u|_0, \quad \|\pi_{i,x}^s\|_0,\|\pi_{i,x}^u\|_0\leq C_1.
nodes.label: eq:app-original-estimates

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem (finite-dimensional characterization)
nodes.statement: Assume first that $f$ satisfies Axiom~A and the strong transversality condition. By Proposition~\ref{stat:uniform-CL-finite}, every derivative sequence admits a $(C_0,\lambda_0)$-structure, with constants independent of the trajectory. On $\Omega(f)$, use the ordinary hyperbolic splitting $ TM|_{\Omega(f)}=E_\Omega^s\oplus E_\Omega^u, $ whose exponential estimates and projection bounds are uniform; denote corresponding constants by $C_\Omega>0$ and $\lambda_\Omega\in(0,1)$. The invariant set $M\setminus\Omega(f)$ contains no periodic points. Choose one representative $p$ from each orbit in this set and write a chosen $(C_0,\lambda_0)$-structure along its derivative sequence as \[ T_{f^k(p)}M=E_k^s\oplus E_k^u,\qquad k\in\mathbb{Z}. \] Define $ E_{f^k(p)}^s:=E_k^s$, $E_{f^k(p)}^u:=E_k^u. $ These definitions are unambiguous because the orbit is nonperiodic. On $\Omega(f)$, set $ E_x^s=E_{\Omega,x}^s$, $ E_x^u=E_{\Omega,x}^u. $ With $ C=\max\{C_0,C_\Omega\}, $ $ \lambda=\max\{\lambda_0,\lambda_\Omega\}, $ the associated projections satisfy {\rm(GH1)}--{\rm(GH3)} on $M$. No continuity of the projections is required. Conversely, assume that $f$ satisfies generalized hyperbolicity. Condition {\rm(GH3)} gives $ E_p^s\subseteq B^+(p)$, $E_p^u\subseteq B^-(p). $ Therefore, \[ T_pM=E_p^s\oplus E_p^u \subseteq B^+(p)+B^-(p) \subseteq T_pM, \] and hence \eqref{eq:app-Mane} holds. By Theorem~\ref{thm:app-Mane}, $f$ is structurally stable. The $C^1$ stability theorem \cite{Mane1987} then implies Axiom~A and the strong transversality condition.
nodes.statement_short: Axiom A + strong transversality: glue Robbin-Robinson orbitwise structures off Omega with the hyperbolic splitting on Omega. Conversely GH gives Mañé's criterion, hence structural stability and Axiom A.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition (elementary properties)
nodes.statement: {\rm(P1)} For $f_1, f_2 \in \mathfrak{D}(\mathbb{B})$ the chain rule gives $\|D(f_1 \circ f_2)(x)\| \leq R_1R_2$ and $ \|D(f_1 \circ f_2)(x+v) - D(f_1 \circ f_2)(x)\| \leq R_1 r_2(|v|) + R_2 r_1(R_2|v|), $ so $f_1 \circ f_2 \in \mathfrak{D}(\mathbb{B})$; in particular $g \in \mathfrak{D}(\mathbb{B})$. The spaces $\tilde E^{s,u}_x = Dh(h^{-1}(x))E^{s,u}_{h^{-1}(x)}$ satisfy {\rm(GH1)}--{\rm(GH3)} for $g$ with constants $R_h^2C$ and $\lambda$. {\rm(P2)} The two inclusions in {\rm(GH2)} and the two estimates in {\rm(GH3)} interchange under $f \to f^{-1}$, $E^s_x \leftrightarrow E^u_x$. {\rm(P3)} Conditions {\rm(GH1)}, {\rm(GH2)} are preserved by iteration, and $|Df^{nm}(x)v^s| \leq C\lambda^{nm}|v^s| = C(\lambda^n)^m|v^s|$. {\rm(P4)} Since $f_i(0) = 0$ and $\|Df_i\| \leq R$, we have $|f_i(x_i)| \leq R|x_i|$, so $f$ maps $\mathbb{B}$ into $\mathbb{B}$; the same applies to $f^{-1}$. Since $r$ is nondecreasing and $|v_i| \leq \|v\|$, $$ \bigl\|\{f_i(x_i+v_i) - f_i(x_i) - Df_i(x_i)v_i\}\bigr\| \leq r(\|v\|)\|v\|, $$ $$ \|Df(x+v) - Df(x)\| = \sup_i \|Df_i(x_i+v_i) - Df_i(x_i)\| \leq r(\|v\|), $$ hence $f \in \mathfrak{D}(\mathbb{B})$ and $Df(x) = \bigoplus_i Df_i(x_i)$. The projections $P_x = \bigoplus_i P^{(i)}_{x_i}$ and $Q_x = \bigoplus_i Q^{(i)}_{x_i}$ are diagonal, so $\|P_x\| = \sup_i \|P^{(i)}_{x_i}\| \leq C$, and {\rm(GH2)}, {\rm(GH3)} hold coordinatewise.
nodes.statement_short: Chain rule and direct verification of (GH1)-(GH3) for conjugates, inverses, iterates and diagonal l^p products.

nodes.name: f and its inverse are well-defined
nodes.statement: By the definition of $f$, the inequalities $|y_{k+1}| \leq R |x_k|$ hold, hence $\|f(\{x_k\})\| \leq R \|\{x_k\}\|$, and $f$ is well-defined. Moreover, $f^{-1}$ is defined by $f^{-1}(\{y_k\}) = \{x_k\}$, where $x_k = a_k^{-1}(y_{k+1})$, with $\|f^{-1}(\{y_k\})\| \leq R\|\{y_k\}\|$; hence $\{x_k\}$ is well-defined.
nodes.statement_short: Bound f and f^{-1} by R to show they are well defined on l^p.
nodes.section: 3.1 Strict invariant inclusions: a nonlinear shift

nodes.name: Linear operator A
nodes.statement: For $\{x_k\} \in \mathbb{B}$ define a linear operator $A(\{x_k\}):\mathbb{B} \to \mathbb{B}$ by $$ A(\{x_k\})\{v_k\} = \{w_k\}, \qquad \mbox{where $w_{k+1} = a'_k(x_k)v_k$}. $$ It is invertible, with $A^{-1}(\{x_k\})\{w_k\} = \{v_k\}$, where $v_k = w_{k+1}/a'_k(x_k)$, and by \eqref{eq:shift-ak} we have $\|A(\{x_k\})\|, \|A^{-1}(\{x_k\})\| \leq R$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the weighted shift A(x) and bound it and its inverse by R.
nodes.section: 3.1 Strict invariant inclusions: a nonlinear shift

nodes.name: Df equals A
nodes.statement: Let us show that $Df(\{x_k\}) = A(\{x_k\})$, where $Df$ is a Fréchet derivative. Indeed, \begin{multline*} f(\{x_k\} + \{v_k\}) - f(\{x_k\}) - A(\{x_k\})\{v_k\} = \{z_k\}, \\ \mbox{where $z_{k+1} = a_k(x_k + v_k) - a_k(x_k) - a'_k(x_k)v_k$}. \end{multline*} According to \eqref{eq:shift-akc2}, we have $|z_k| \leq M|v_k|^2$ and hence inequality \eqref{eq:C1-1} holds with $r(|v|) = M|v|$. Similarly, equation \eqref{eq:C1-r1} holds and $r$ satisfies \eqref{eq:C1-r2}.
nodes.statement_short: Show the Fréchet derivative is A and the C^1 conditions hold.
nodes.section: 3.1 Strict invariant inclusions: a nonlinear shift

nodes.name: Remainder computation
nodes.statement: Indeed, \begin{multline*} f(\{x_k\} + \{v_k\}) - f(\{x_k\}) - A(\{x_k\})\{v_k\} = \{z_k\}, \\ \mbox{where $z_{k+1} = a_k(x_k + v_k) - a_k(x_k) - a'_k(x_k)v_k$}. \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Write the remainder coordinatewise.
nodes.section: 3.1 Strict invariant inclusions: a nonlinear shift

nodes.name: C^1 conditions
nodes.statement: According to \eqref{eq:shift-akc2}, we have $|z_k| \leq M|v_k|^2$ and hence inequality \eqref{eq:C1-1} holds with $r(|v|) = M|v|$. Similarly, equation \eqref{eq:C1-r1} holds and $r$ satisfies \eqref{eq:C1-r2}.
nodes.statement_short: Quadratic remainder bound gives (C1-1), (C1-r1), (C1-r2).
nodes.section: 3.1 Strict invariant inclusions: a nonlinear shift

nodes.name: Verify GH1-GH3
nodes.statement: Let us show that $f$ satisfies generalized hyperbolicity. Denote $$ E^s = \{ v_k = 0, k < 0 \}, \quad E^u = \{ v_k = 0, k \geq 0 \}. $$ Note that $E^s \oplus E^u = \mathbb{B}$. Let $P_x, Q_x$ be the projections onto $E^s$ and $E^u$ respectively (independent of $x$). Then $ E^s_x = P_x(\mathbb{B}) = E^s$, $E^u_x = Q_x(\mathbb{B}) = E^u$, and $\|P_x\| = \|Q_x\| = 1 $, so condition (GH1) holds with $C \geq 1$. By construction, $A(x)E^s \subset E^s$ and $A^{-1}(x)E^u \subset E^u$, hence condition (GH2) holds. By \eqref{eq:shift-ak} we have $\|A(x)|_{E^s}\|, \|A^{-1}(x)|_{E^u}\| \leq \lambda$, and hence condition (GH3) holds with $C = 1$ and the same $\lambda$ as above.
nodes.statement_short: Check (GH1)-(GH3) for the constant coordinate splitting.
nodes.section: 3.1 Strict invariant inclusions: a nonlinear shift

nodes.name: Coordinate splitting and GH1
nodes.statement: Denote $$ E^s = \{ v_k = 0, k < 0 \}, \quad E^u = \{ v_k = 0, k \geq 0 \}. $$ Note that $E^s \oplus E^u = \mathbb{B}$. Let $P_x, Q_x$ be the projections onto $E^s$ and $E^u$ respectively (independent of $x$). Then $ E^s_x = P_x(\mathbb{B}) = E^s$, $E^u_x = Q_x(\mathbb{B}) = E^u$, and $\|P_x\| = \|Q_x\| = 1 $, so condition (GH1) holds with $C \geq 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Coordinate splitting with norm-one projections gives (GH1).
nodes.section: 3.1 Strict invariant inclusions: a nonlinear shift

nodes.name: GH2
nodes.statement: By construction, $A(x)E^s \subset E^s$ and $A^{-1}(x)E^u \subset E^u$, hence condition (GH2) holds.
nodes.statement_short: A maps E^s into E^s and A^{-1} maps E^u into E^u.
nodes.section: 3.1 Strict invariant inclusions: a nonlinear shift

nodes.name: GH3
nodes.statement: By \eqref{eq:shift-ak} we have $\|A(x)|_{E^s}\|, \|A^{-1}(x)|_{E^u}\| \leq \lambda$, and hence condition (GH3) holds with $C = 1$ and the same $\lambda$ as above.
nodes.statement_short: Contraction rates give (GH3) with C=1.
nodes.section: 3.1 Strict invariant inclusions: a nonlinear shift

nodes.name: a belongs to D(R)
nodes.statement: By \eqref{eq:aLip}, the map $a$ satisfies \eqref{eq:C1-2} with $R = 1/\lambda_1$ and \eqref{eq:C1-r1} with $r(t) = Mt$, and this $r$ satisfies \eqref{eq:C1-r2}; hence $a \in \mathfrak{D}(\mathbb{R})$.
nodes.statement_short: Derivative bounds put a in D(R).
nodes.section: 3.2 Discontinuous splittings and varying index: products of Morse-Smale maps

nodes.name: GH of a
nodes.statement: As explained above, $a$ satisfies generalized hyperbolicity with constants $C = (\lambda_1\lambda_2)^{-n_0}$, $\lambda = \lambda_2$ and the splitting $\mathbb{R} = G^s_x \oplus G^u_x$.
nodes.statement_short: Recall GH of the one-dimensional map a.
nodes.section: 3.2 Discontinuous splittings and varying index: products of Morse-Smale maps

nodes.name: Apply (P4)
nodes.statement: Since $a(0) = 0$ and $$ \mathbb{B} = \ell^p(\mathbb{Z}) = \Bigl(\bigoplus_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} \mathbb{R}\Bigr)_{\ell^p}, $$ Proposition~\ref{stat:difconj}\,{\rm(P4)}, applied with $\mathbb{B}_k = \mathbb{R}$ and $f_k = a$ for every $k \in \mathbb{Z}$, shows that $f \in \mathfrak{D}(\mathbb{B})$, that $Df(\{x_k\})\{v_k\} = \{a'(x_k)v_k\}$, and that $f$ satisfies generalized hyperbolicity with the same constants $C$ and $\lambda$, with respect to the splitting $$ E^s_x = \bigoplus_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} G_{x_k}^s = \{v_k = 0, \mbox{if $|x_k| \leq 1/2$}\}, \qquad E^u_x = \bigoplus_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} G_{x_k}^u = \{v_k = 0, \mbox{if $|x_k| > 1/2$}\} $$ and the corresponding projections $P_x$, $Q_x$.
nodes.statement_short: Proposition (P4) transfers membership in D and GH to the l^p product.
nodes.section: 3.2 Discontinuous splittings and varying index: products of Morse-Smale maps

nodes.name: Trapping neighbourhoods
nodes.statement: By \eqref{eq:3-3-1}, there exist $\lambda \in (0, 1)$ and interval neighborhoods $U_s$ of $s$ and $U_u$ of $u$ such that \begin{equation} g(U_s) \subset U_s, \quad a(x) < \lambda \quad x \in U_s, \end{equation} \begin{equation} g^{-1}(U_u) \subset U_u, \quad a(x) > 1/\lambda \quad x \in U_u. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Choose trapping neighbourhoods U_s, U_u with weight below lambda / above 1/lambda.

nodes.name: Case L^p
nodes.statement: \textbf{Case 1.} $\mathbb{B} = L^p(\mathbb{S}^1, \mathbb{R})$ with $p \in [1, +\infty]$. Set $b_p(x):=a(x)|g'(x)|^{1/p}$, and set $b_\infty:=a$. Since $s$ and $u$ are hyperbolic attracting and repelling fixed points, respectively, $b_p(s)<1$, $b_p(u)>1$. For $p<+\infty$, a change of variables gives $$ |Tv|_p^p=\int_{\mathbb S^1} b_p(x)^p|v(x)|^p\,dx, $$ so $b_p$ is the effective weight for the $L^p$ estimates. Decreasing the neighborhoods $U_s,U_u$, while preserving the inclusions in \eqref{eq:3-3-s}, \eqref{eq:3-3-u}, we can assume that there exists $\lambda_p\in(0,1)$ such that $$ b_p(x)<\lambda_p\quad(x\in U_s), \qquad b_p(x)>\lambda_p^{-1}\quad(x\in U_u). $$ Let $\xi_1,\xi_2$ be the boundary points of $U_u$, set $V=\mathbb S^1\setminus U_u$, and choose $N>1$ such that $g^N(V)\subset U_s$. Define the projections $P, Q: \mathbb{B} \to \mathbb{B}$ by $$ Pv(x) = \begin{cases} v(x), & \quad x \in V, \\ 0, & \quad x \in U_u; \end{cases} \quad Qv(x) = \begin{cases} 0, & \quad x \in V, \\ v(x), & \quad x \in U_u, \end{cases} $$ and set $E^s := P(\mathbb{B})$, $E^u := Q(\mathbb{B})$. Note that \begin{equation} g(V) \subset V, \quad g^{-1}(U_u) \subset U_u, \quad V \cup U_u = \mathbb{S}^1. \end{equation} Hence $TE^s \subset E^s$, $T^{-1}E^u \subset E^u$, $P+Q = Id$. For a suitable global bound $R_p\geq1$ on $b_p$ and $b_p^{-1}$, set $C_p=(R_p/\lambda_p)^N$. The choice of $U_s,U_u,V,N$ and \eqref{eq:3-3-incl} imply that \begin{equation} |T^n v^s| \leq C_p\lambda_p^{n}|v^s|, \quad v^s \in E^s, n > 0; \end{equation} \begin{equation} |T^{-n} v^u| \leq C_p\lambda_p^{n}|v^u|, \quad v^u \in E^u, n > 0, \end{equation} and $T$ is generalized hyperbolic with the splitting $\mathbb{B} = E^s \oplus E^u$.
nodes.statement_short: L^p case: cut-off projections onto V and U_u.

nodes.name: Effective weight
nodes.statement: \textbf{Case 1.} $\mathbb{B} = L^p(\mathbb{S}^1, \mathbb{R})$ with $p \in [1, +\infty]$. Set $b_p(x):=a(x)|g'(x)|^{1/p}$, and set $b_\infty:=a$. Since $s$ and $u$ are hyperbolic attracting and repelling fixed points, respectively, $b_p(s)<1$, $b_p(u)>1$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the effective L^p weight b_p.

nodes.name: Change of variables
nodes.statement: For $p<+\infty$, a change of variables gives $$ |Tv|_p^p=\int_{\mathbb S^1} b_p(x)^p|v(x)|^p\,dx, $$ so $b_p$ is the effective weight for the $L^p$ estimates.
nodes.statement_short: The L^p norm of Tv is a b_p-weighted integral.

nodes.name: Shrink neighbourhoods
