Hence, $$ v^s_x - A^{-1}(x) H^u_x A(x) H^s_x v^s_x = v^s_x + v^u_x - A^{-1}(x)(v^u_{\alpha(x)} + v^s_{\alpha(x)}) \in \tilde{E}^s_x \oplus A^{-1}(x)\tilde{E}^u_{\beta(x)}. $$ Note that for $\varepsilon < 1/R$ the following holds $$ A^{-1}(x) H^u_x A(x) H^s_x (E^s_x) \subset E^s_x, \quad \|A^{-1}(x) H^u_x A(x) H^s_x\| < 1, $$ hence $Id - A^{-1}(x) H^u_x A(x) H^s_x$ is bijective on $E^s_x$. In particular $ E^s_x \subset \tilde{E}^s_x \oplus A^{-1}(x)\tilde{E}^u_{\beta(x)} $. Similarly, we show $ F_x = A^{-1}(x)E^u_{\alpha(x)} \subset \tilde{E}^s_x \oplus A^{-1}(x)\tilde{E}^u_{\beta(x)} $, and hence $ E^s_x \oplus F_x \subset \tilde{E}^s_x \oplus A^{-1}(x)\tilde{E}^u_{\beta(x)} $, which together with inclusion \eqref{eq:tildeE-EF-1} implies \eqref{eq:tildeE-EF}.
nodes.statement_short: Show E~s + A^{-1}E~u = E^s + F by two inclusions.

nodes.name: First inclusion
nodes.statement: According to construction $\tilde{E}^s_x \subset E^s_x \oplus F_x$ and \begin{align*} A^{-1}(x)\tilde{E}^u_{\beta(x)} & \subset A^{-1}(x)E^u_{\alpha(x)} \oplus A^{-1}(x)A(x)E^s_x = E^s_x \oplus F_x. \end{align*} Hence, \begin{equation} \tilde{E}^s_x \oplus A^{-1}(x)\tilde{E}^u_{\beta(x)} \subset E^s_x \oplus F_x. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Both new subspaces lie in E^s + F.

nodes.name: Auxiliary vectors
nodes.statement: For any $x \in \mathbb{B}$ and $v^s_x \in E^s_x$ define the vectors $$ v^u_x := H^s_xv^s_x \in F_x = A^{-1}(x)E^u_{\alpha(x)}, \quad v^u_{\alpha(x)} := A(x)v^u_x \in E^u_{\alpha(x)}, \quad v^s_{\alpha(x)} := H^u_x v^u_{\alpha(x)} \in A(x)E_x^s. $$ Then $v^s_x + v^u_x \in \tilde{E}^s_x$ and $v^u_{\alpha(x)} + v^s_{\alpha(x)} \in \tilde{E}^u_{\beta(x)}$. Hence, $$ v^s_x - A^{-1}(x) H^u_x A(x) H^s_x v^s_x = v^s_x + v^u_x - A^{-1}(x)(v^u_{\alpha(x)} + v^s_{\alpha(x)}) \in \tilde{E}^s_x \oplus A^{-1}(x)\tilde{E}^u_{\beta(x)}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Build elements of the new sum from v^s via H^s and H^u.

nodes.name: Neumann argument
nodes.statement: Note that for $\varepsilon < 1/R$ the following holds $$ A^{-1}(x) H^u_x A(x) H^s_x (E^s_x) \subset E^s_x, \quad \|A^{-1}(x) H^u_x A(x) H^s_x\| < 1, $$ hence $Id - A^{-1}(x) H^u_x A(x) H^s_x$ is bijective on $E^s_x$. In particular $ E^s_x \subset \tilde{E}^s_x \oplus A^{-1}(x)\tilde{E}^u_{\beta(x)} $.
nodes.statement_short: A small operator on E^s makes Id - K bijective, so E^s lies in the new sum.

nodes.name: Second inclusion
nodes.statement: Similarly, we show $ F_x = A^{-1}(x)E^u_{\alpha(x)} \subset \tilde{E}^s_x \oplus A^{-1}(x)\tilde{E}^u_{\beta(x)} $, and hence $ E^s_x \oplus F_x \subset \tilde{E}^s_x \oplus A^{-1}(x)\tilde{E}^u_{\beta(x)} $, which together with inclusion \eqref{eq:tildeE-EF-1} implies \eqref{eq:tildeE-EF}.
nodes.statement_short: Likewise F lies in the new sum; equality follows.

nodes.name: Cocycle (f, Df)
nodes.statement: Assume that $f$ satisfies uniformly continuous generalized hyperbolicity with constants $C > 0$, $\lambda \in (0, 1)$. Then the pair $(f, Df)$ satisfies uniformly continuous cocycle generalized hyperbolicity.
nodes.statement_short: The pair (f, Df) has uniformly continuous cocycle GH.

nodes.name: Constants
nodes.statement: Let $\varepsilon_0$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:SS2}. Choose $\varepsilon_1 \in (0,\varepsilon_0)$ and $\lambda_1\in(\lambda,1)$, and let $C_1>1$ and $\delta>0$ be the corresponding constants. Let $R > 1$ be the constant in \eqref{eq:C1-2}, $L = L(C_1, \lambda_1)>0$ be the constant provided by Lemma \ref{lem:SS1}. Set $\varepsilon=\frac{1}{3L}$. Choose $d_0 < \min(\frac{\delta}{R}, \frac{1}{3L})$, such that \eqref{eq:s-Lip} holds with this $\varepsilon$ for $|v_1|, |v_2| < 2Ld_0$. Fix $d\in(0,d_0)$ and $g\in\mathfrak{D}(\mathbb{B})$ satisfying $\|g-f\|_{C^1}<d$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix epsilon_1, lambda_1, C_1, delta, L, epsilon = 1/(3L), d_0, d and g.

nodes.name: Perturbation Delta
nodes.statement: Denote $\Delta = g - f$. Then \begin{equation} |\Delta(x)| < d, \quad \|D\Delta(x)\| < d, \quad x \in \mathbb{B}. \end{equation} Moreover, for every $x\in\mathbb{B}$, setting $y=g^{-1}(x)$, we have \[ |f^{-1}(x)-g^{-1}(x)| = |f^{-1}(g(y))-f^{-1}(f(y))| \leq R|g(y)-f(y)| <Rd<\delta. \] Together with $\sup_x|f(x)-g(x)|<d<\delta$, this verifies \eqref{eq:al-be-ep}.
nodes.statement_short: Delta is C^1-small and the base maps satisfy the closeness hypothesis of Lemma SS2.

nodes.name: Cocycle (g, Df)
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lem:SS2}, the pair $(g, Df)$ satisfies uniformly continuous cocycle generalized hyperbolicity with constants~$C_1, \lambda_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma SS2 gives cocycle GH for (g, Df).

nodes.name: Splittings
nodes.statement: Denote the splitting corresponding to the pair $(f, Df)$ by $$ \mathbb{B} = E^s_x \oplus E^u_x, \quad F_x = (Df(x))^{-1}E^u_{f(x)} \subset E^u_x $$ and splitting provided by Lemma \ref{lem:SS2} corresponding to pair $(g, Df)$ by \begin{equation}\notag \mathbb{B} = \tilde{E}^s_x \oplus \tilde{E}^u_x, \quad \tilde{F}_x = (Df(x))^{-1}\tilde{E}^u_{g(x)} \subset \tilde{E}^u_x. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Name the splittings for (f,Df) and (g,Df).

nodes.name: Remark on (g, Dg)
nodes.statement: \begin{remark} We do not claim that the pair $(g, Dg)$ satisfies uniformly continuous cocycle generalized hyperbolicity, although we believe it to be true. \end{remark}
nodes.statement_short: Remark: GH of (g, Dg) is not claimed.

nodes.name: Common space Y and inverses
nodes.statement: According to \eqref{eq:tildeE-EF} the following equality holds $ \tilde{E}^s_x \oplus \tilde{F}_x = {E}^s_x \oplus {F}_x. $ Hence $$ \{v \in X: v(x) \in \tilde{E}_x^s \oplus \tilde{F}_x\} = Y. $$ By Lemma \ref{lem:SS1} there exist operators $O_f, O_g: X \to Y$ satisfying $$ T_{f, Df}O_f = Id_X, \; \|O_f\| \leq L, \quad T_{g, Df}O_g = Id_X, \; \|O_g\| \leq L. $$ Denote $M = 2L$.
nodes.statement_short: Both cocycles share the space Y; Lemma SS1 gives inverses O_f, O_g.

nodes.name: Step 1: h_1
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step 1.} First, we find a map $h_1: \mathbb{B} \to \mathbb{B}$, $h_1 \in Y$, satisfying \eqref{eq:conj-h1}. Substituting $g = f + \Delta$ in equation \eqref{eq:conj-h1} and using the definition of $s_f$ we get $$ f(x) + Df(x)h_1(x) + s_f(x, h_1(x)) + \Delta(x+h_1(x)) = f(x) + h_1(f(x)), \quad x \in \mathbb{B}. $$ Canceling $f(x)$ and regrouping terms we get \begin{equation} h_1(f(x)) = Df(x)h_1(x) + s_f(x, h_1(x)) + \Delta(x+h_1(x)), \quad x \in \mathbb{B}. \end{equation} In order for \eqref{eq:conj-final} to hold, it suffices that \begin{equation} h_1(x) = O_f(s_f(x, h_1(x)) + \Delta(x+h_1(x))). \end{equation} Consider the (nonlinear) operator $G_f:BUC(\mathbb{B}, \mathbb{B}) \to BUC(\mathbb{B}, \mathbb{B})$ defined by $$ G_f(h_1)(x) = s_f(x, h_1(x)) + \Delta(x+h_1(x)), \quad x \in \mathbb{B}. $$ Using \eqref{eq:s-Lip} and \eqref{eq:Delta-c1} we conclude that for $|h_1|, |h'_1| \leq 2L d$ the following inequalities hold \begin{multline*} |(G_f(h_1)-G_f(h'_1))(x)| = |s_f(x, h_1(x)) - s_f(x, h'_1(x)) + \Delta(x+h_1(x)) - \Delta(x+h'_1(x))| \leq \\ (\varepsilon+d)|h_1(x) - h'_1(x)| \leq \frac{2}{3L}\|h_1 - h'_1\|. \end{multline*} Using \eqref{eq:Sf} we conclude that $ \|O_f \circ G_f(h_1) - O_f \circ G_f(h'_1)\| \leq \frac{2}{3}\|h_1-h'_1\|, $ hence $O_f \circ G_f$ is a contraction. For $\|h_1\| \leq 2Ld$, equations \eqref{eq:s-Lip}, \eqref{eq:Delta-c1} imply $\|G_f(h_1)\| \leq \varepsilon 2Ld + d$, and $$ \|O_f \circ G_f(h_1)\| \leq L(\varepsilon \cdot 2Ld + d) = \left(\frac{2L}{3}+L\right)d \leq 2Ld. $$ The latter implies existence and uniqueness of a map $h_1$ with $\|h_1\| \leq 2Ld$ satisfying $O_f \circ G_f (h_1) = h_1$, and hence \eqref{eq:conj-h1}. Therefore $h_1$ satisfies \eqref{eq:h1h2leqMdelta}. Note that $\mbox{Im }O_f = Y$ and hence $h_1 \in Y$.
nodes.statement_short: Find h_1 in Y as fixed point of the contraction O_f o G_f.

nodes.name: Step 2: h_2
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step 2.} To construct a map $h_2 \in Y$, satisfying \eqref{eq:conj-h2} we follow an approach similar to that of Step 1. For completeness, we provide the full proof below. The conjugacy \eqref{eq:conj-h2} is equivalent to $$ f(x+h_2(x)) = f(x) + \Delta(x) + h_2(g(x)), \quad x \in \mathbb{B}. $$ Using definition of $s_f$ and canceling $f(x)$ we get \begin{equation} h_2(g(x)) = Df(x)h_2(x) + s_f(x, h_2(x)) + \Delta(x), \quad x \in \mathbb{B}. \end{equation} In order for \eqref{eq:conj-final-g} to hold, it suffices that \begin{equation} h_2(x) = O_g(s_f(x, h_2(x)) + \Delta(x)). \end{equation} Consider the (nonlinear) operator $G_g:BUC(\mathbb{B}, \mathbb{B}) \to BUC(\mathbb{B}, \mathbb{B})$ defined by $$ G_g(h_2)(x) = s_f(x, h_2(x)) + \Delta(x), \quad x \in \mathbb{B}. $$ Using \eqref{eq:s-Lip} and \eqref{eq:Delta-c1} we conclude that for $|h_2|, |h'_2| \leq 2L d$ the following inequalities hold \begin{multline*} |(G_g(h_2)-G_g(h'_2))(x)| = |s_f(x, h_2(x)) - s_f(x, h'_2(x))| \leq \varepsilon|h_2(x) - h'_2(x)| \leq \frac{1}{3L}\|h_2 - h'_2\|. \end{multline*} Using \eqref{eq:Sf} we conclude that $ \|O_g \circ G_g(h_2) - O_g \circ G_g(h'_2)\| \leq \frac{1}{3}\|h_2-h'_2\| $ and hence $O_g \circ G_g$ is a contraction. If $\|h_2\| \leq 2Ld$ then \eqref{eq:s-Lip} and \eqref{eq:Delta-c1} imply $\|G_g(h_2)\| \leq \varepsilon 2Ld + d$, and $$ \|O_g \circ G_g(h_2)\| \leq L(\varepsilon \cdot 2Ld + d) = \left(\frac{2L}{3}+L\right)d \leq 2Ld. $$ The latter implies existence and uniqueness of a map $h_2$ with $\|h_2\| \leq 2Ld$ satisfying $ O_g \circ G_g (h_2) = h_2, $ and hence \eqref{eq:conj-final-g}. Therefore, $h_2$ satisfies \eqref{eq:conj-h2} and \eqref{eq:h1h2leqMdelta}. Note that $\mbox{Im }O_g = Y$, hence $h_2 \in Y$. This proves Theorem~\ref{thm:SS}\,(\ref{item:SS-semi}).
nodes.statement_short: Find h_2 in Y as fixed point of the contraction O_g o G_g.

nodes.name: Step 3: inverse maps
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step 3.} Under the additional assumption in Theorem~\ref{thm:SS}\,(\ref{item:SS-full}), we prove \eqref{eq:Idh-homeo}. From \eqref{eq:conj-h1} and \eqref{eq:conj-h2} we obtain the following. \begin{equation} f \circ (Id+h_2) \circ (Id+h_1) = (Id+h_2) \circ (Id+h_1) \circ f, \end{equation} \begin{equation} g \circ (Id+h_1) \circ (Id+h_2) = (Id+h_1) \circ (Id+h_2) \circ g. \end{equation} Since $h_1, h_2 \in Y$ and the spaces $E^s_x \oplus (Df(x))^{-1}E^u_{f(x)} = E^s_x \oplus F_x$ do not depend on $x$, for some functions $h_3, h_4 \in Y$ the following hold $$ (Id+h_2) \circ (Id+h_1) = Id + h_3, \quad (Id+h_1) \circ (Id+h_2) = Id + h_4. $$ \begin{equation} h_3(x), h_4(x) \in E^s_x \oplus F_x, \quad |h_3(x)|, |h_4(x)| \leq 2Md, \quad x \in \mathbb{B}. \end{equation} By \eqref{eq:selff} the identity $ f\circ (Id+h_3) = (Id+h_3) \circ f $ holds. Arguing as in Step~1, we conclude that $$ h_3(f(x)) - Df(x)h_3(x) = s_f(x, h_3(x)). $$ Since $h_3 \in Y$, Lemma \ref{lem:SS1} implies that \begin{equation} h_3 = O_f(s_f(x, h_3(x))). \end{equation} Similarly to the operator $O_f \circ G_f$, the map $h_3 \to O_f(s_f(x, h_3(x)))$ is a contraction (decreasing $d$ if necessary) on the set of $h_3$ with $\|h_3\| \leq 2Md$. Therefore, equation \eqref{eq:h3-fixed} has a unique solution for $h_3$ satisfying \eqref{eq:h3h4-cond}. On the other hand, $h_3 \equiv 0$ satisfies both \eqref{eq:h3h4-cond} and \eqref{eq:h3-fixed}. By uniqueness $h_3 \equiv 0$. The argument for $h_4$ is analogous. Equation \eqref{eq:selfg} implies that $g \circ (Id+h_4) = (Id+h_4) \circ g$. Arguing as in Step~2, we obtain $$ h_4(g(x)) - Df(x)h_4(x) = s_f(x, h_4(x)) + \left( \Delta(x+h_4(x)) - \Delta(x) \right). $$ As in the proof for $h_3$, this equation has a unique solution $h_4$, satisfying \eqref{eq:h3h4-cond}. Hence, $h_4 \equiv 0$. This completes the proof of \eqref{eq:Idh-homeo} and Theorem \ref{thm:SS}\,(\ref{item:SS-full}).
nodes.statement_short: Uniqueness of fixed points forces h_3 = h_4 = 0.

nodes.name: Self-conjugacies
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step 3.} Under the additional assumption in Theorem~\ref{thm:SS}\,(\ref{item:SS-full}), we prove \eqref{eq:Idh-homeo}. From \eqref{eq:conj-h1} and \eqref{eq:conj-h2} we obtain the following. \begin{equation} f \circ (Id+h_2) \circ (Id+h_1) = (Id+h_2) \circ (Id+h_1) \circ f, \end{equation} \begin{equation} g \circ (Id+h_1) \circ (Id+h_2) = (Id+h_1) \circ (Id+h_2) \circ g. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Compose the semi-conjugacies to get self-conjugacies of f and g.

nodes.name: h_3, h_4 in Y
nodes.statement: Since $h_1, h_2 \in Y$ and the spaces $E^s_x \oplus (Df(x))^{-1}E^u_{f(x)} = E^s_x \oplus F_x$ do not depend on $x$, for some functions $h_3, h_4 \in Y$ the following hold $$ (Id+h_2) \circ (Id+h_1) = Id + h_3, \quad (Id+h_1) \circ (Id+h_2) = Id + h_4. $$ \begin{equation} h_3(x), h_4(x) \in E^s_x \oplus F_x, \quad |h_3(x)|, |h_4(x)| \leq 2Md, \quad x \in \mathbb{B}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Constancy of E^s + F keeps h_3, h_4 in Y with norm 2Md.

nodes.name: Fixed-point equation for h_3
nodes.statement: By \eqref{eq:selff} the identity $ f\circ (Id+h_3) = (Id+h_3) \circ f $ holds. Arguing as in Step~1, we conclude that $$ h_3(f(x)) - Df(x)h_3(x) = s_f(x, h_3(x)). $$ Since $h_3 \in Y$, Lemma \ref{lem:SS1} implies that \begin{equation} h_3 = O_f(s_f(x, h_3(x))). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: h_3 solves a fixed-point equation via Lemma SS1.

nodes.name: h_3 = 0
nodes.statement: Similarly to the operator $O_f \circ G_f$, the map $h_3 \to O_f(s_f(x, h_3(x)))$ is a contraction (decreasing $d$ if necessary) on the set of $h_3$ with $\|h_3\| \leq 2Md$. Therefore, equation \eqref{eq:h3-fixed} has a unique solution for $h_3$ satisfying \eqref{eq:h3h4-cond}. On the other hand, $h_3 \equiv 0$ satisfies both \eqref{eq:h3h4-cond} and \eqref{eq:h3-fixed}. By uniqueness $h_3 \equiv 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Contraction uniqueness and the zero solution give h_3 = 0.

nodes.name: h_4 = 0
nodes.statement: The argument for $h_4$ is analogous. Equation \eqref{eq:selfg} implies that $g \circ (Id+h_4) = (Id+h_4) \circ g$. Arguing as in Step~2, we obtain $$ h_4(g(x)) - Df(x)h_4(x) = s_f(x, h_4(x)) + \left( \Delta(x+h_4(x)) - \Delta(x) \right). $$ As in the proof for $h_3$, this equation has a unique solution $h_4$, satisfying \eqref{eq:h3h4-cond}. Hence, $h_4 \equiv 0$. This completes the proof of \eqref{eq:Idh-homeo} and Theorem \ref{thm:SS}\,(\ref{item:SS-full}).
nodes.statement_short: Similarly h_4 = 0, so the maps are mutually inverse.

nodes.name: Blocks and finite shadowing
nodes.statement: Fix an integer $m \ge 4L$ and set $ n_k := \frac{k(k-1)}{2}m $, so that $n_0 = n_1 = 0$ and $n_{k+1} - n_k = km$ for $k \ge 1$; the intervals $[n_k, n_{k+1})$, $k \ge 1$, partition $[0, +\infty) \cap \mathbb{Z}$. For each $k \ge 1$ the restriction $\{x_j\}_{|j| \le n_{k+1}}$ is a finite $d$-pseudotrajectory, so by the finite Lipschitz shadowing property there is $u_k \in X$ with \begin{equation} \|x_j - T^j u_k\| \le Ld \qquad (|j| \le n_{k+1}). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Partition into blocks of length km and shadow finite pieces by u_k.

nodes.name: Linear interpolation
nodes.statement: We interpolate linearly between consecutive shadowing points. For $j \ge 0$ write $j = n_k + i$ with $k \ge 1$ and $0 \le i < km$, and put $$ x'_j := \Big(1 - \tfrac{i}{km}\Big) T^j u_k + \tfrac{i}{km}\, T^j u_{k+1}; $$ for $j < 0$ write $-j = n_k + i$ in the same way and put $x'_j := \big(1 - \tfrac{i}{km}\big) T^j u_k + \tfrac{i}{km}\, T^j u_{k+1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Define x' by interpolating T^j u_k and T^j u_{k+1}.

nodes.name: Displacement
nodes.statement: \textbf{Displacement.} Let $j \ge 0$, $j = n_k + i$. Then $j \le n_{k+1} \le n_{k+2}$, so \eqref{eq:BP-uk} holds at $j$ both for $u_k$ and for $u_{k+1}$; as $x'_j$ is a convex combination of $T^j u_k$ and $T^j u_{k+1}$, $$ \|x_j - x'_j\| \le \Big(1-\tfrac{i}{km}\Big)\|x_j - T^j u_k\| + \tfrac{i}{km}\,\|x_j - T^j u_{k+1}\| \le Ld. $$ The case $j<0$ is identical, so $\|x_j - x'_j\| \le Ld$ for all $j \in \mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.statement_short: Convex combination keeps x' within Ld of x.

nodes.name: Halved error
nodes.statement: \textbf{Halved error.} Let $j \ge 0$, $j = n_k + i$ with $0 \le i < km$. If $i+1 \le km-1$, then $j+1$ lies in the same block and a direct computation gives $$ Tx'_j - x'_{j+1} = \tfrac{1}{km}\big(T^{j+1}u_k - T^{j+1}u_{k+1}\big). $$ If $i+1 = km$, then $j+1 = n_{k+1}$ is the first index of the next block, where $x'_{j+1} = T^{j+1}u_{k+1}$, and the same identity follows since $x'_j = \tfrac{1}{km}T^{j}u_k + \big(1-\tfrac{1}{km}\big)T^{j}u_{k+1}$ in this case. In either case $j+1 \le n_{k+1} \le n_{k+2}$, so \eqref{eq:BP-uk} applies at $j+1$ for both $u_k$ and $u_{k+1}$, and therefore $$ \|Tx'_j - x'_{j+1}\| \le \tfrac{1}{km}\Big(\|T^{j+1}u_k - x_{j+1}\| + \|x_{j+1} - T^{j+1}u_{k+1}\|\Big) \le \frac{2Ld}{km} \le \frac{2Ld}{m} \le \frac{d}{2}, $$ where we used $k \ge 1$ and $m \ge 4L$. The estimate for $j < 0$, including the junction between $j=-1$ and $j=0$, is analogous. Hence, $\{x'_j\}$ is a $\tfrac{d}{2}$-pseudotrajectory.
nodes.statement_short: The one-step error is at most 2Ld/(km) <= d/2.

nodes.name: Iterate halving
nodes.statement: Let $\{x_j\}_{j \in \mathbb{Z}}$ be a $d$-pseudotrajectory of $T$. Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:halving} repeatedly, we construct pseudotrajectories $\{x^{(l)}_j\}_{j \in \mathbb{Z}}$, $l \ge 0$, with $x^{(0)}_j = x_j$ and, for every $l \ge 0$, $$ \{x^{(l+1)}_j\}\ \text{is a}\ \tfrac{d}{2^{l+1}}\text{-pseudotrajectory}, \qquad \|x^{(l+1)}_j - x^{(l)}_j\| \le L\,\frac{d}{2^{l}} \quad (j \in \mathbb{Z}), $$ where the displacement bound uses that $\{x^{(l)}_j\}$ is a $\tfrac{d}{2^{l}}$-pseudotrajectory.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the halving lemma repeatedly.

nodes.name: Limit is exact
nodes.statement: Fix $j \in \mathbb{Z}$. The bound $\|x^{(l+1)}_j - x^{(l)}_j\| \le Ld\,2^{-l}$ shows that $\big(x^{(l)}_j\big)_{l \ge 0}$ is a Cauchy sequence in $X$; let $v_j := \lim_{l \to \infty} x^{(l)}_j$. Letting $l \to \infty$ in $\|Tx^{(l)}_j - x^{(l)}_{j+1}\| \le d\,2^{-l}$ yields $Tv_j = v_{j+1}$, so $\{v_j\}$ is an exact trajectory, that is, $v_j = T^j v$ with $v := v_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy limits form an exact trajectory.

nodes.name: Constant 2L
nodes.statement: Finally, $$ \|x_j - T^j v\| = \|x^{(0)}_j - v_j\| \le \sum_{l \ge 0} \|x^{(l)}_j - x^{(l+1)}_j\| \le \sum_{l \ge 0} L\,\frac{d}{2^{l}} = 2Ld. $$ As $j \in \mathbb{Z}$ was arbitrary, $T$ has the Lipschitz shadowing property with constant $2L$.
nodes.statement_short: Sum the displacements to get 2Ld.

nodes.name: Uniformity
nodes.statement: The constants in this statement are independent of the trajectory. We recall the ingredients of the Robbin--Robinson construction responsible for this uniformity.
nodes.statement_short: Recall the ingredients giving uniform constants.

nodes.name: Adapted metric
nodes.statement: \textbf{Adapted metric.} Let $|\cdot|_0$ denote the norm of the Riemannian metric fixed above. Since $\Omega(f)$ is hyperbolic, the standard adapted-metric construction gives a continuous Riemannian norm $|\cdot|_*$ and a number $\theta_0\in(0,1)$ such that \[ |Df(x)v^s|_*\leq\theta_0|v^s|_*, \qquad |D(f^{-1})(x)v^u|_*\leq\theta_0|v^u|_* \] for $x\in\Omega(f)$, $v^s\in E_{\Omega,x}^s$, and $v^u\in E_{\Omega,x}^u$. Extend this metric to $M$. Robinson's compatible-bundle construction then provides neighborhoods of the basic sets and a number $\theta\in(\theta_0,1)$ for which the one-step estimates in Proposition~\ref{stat:Robinson-bundles} hold. This is the adapted metric used in Robinson's construction; see the proof of Theorem~5.1 in \cite{Robinson1976}. Since $M$ is compact, the two norms are uniformly equivalent: there is $\kappa\geq1$ such that \begin{equation} \kappa^{-1}|v|_0\leq|v|_*\leq\kappa|v|_0, \qquad v\in TM. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Adapted metric on Omega, extended to M, equivalent to the original with constant kappa.

nodes.name: Compatible bundles
nodes.statement: \textbf{Compatible bundles.} Let $ \Omega(f)=\Omega_1\cup\cdots\cup\Omega_m $ be the spectral decomposition. In the notation of this paper, Proposition~7.1 of \cite[p.~66]{Robinson1976} gives the following statement with respect to the adapted metric. \begin{statement}[Robinson, Proposition~7.1] There exist neighborhoods $Z_i$ of $\Omega_i$, continuous subbundles $E_i^u,E_i^s$ of $TM|_{\mathcal O(Z_i)}$, $i=1,\ldots,m$, and $\theta\in(0,1)$ such that: \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] $E_i^u$ and $E_i^s$ are invariant under $Df$; \item[(2)] if $x\in\mathcal O^+(Z_j)\cap\mathcal O^-(Z_i)$, then $ E_{i,x}^u\subseteq E_{j,x}^u$, $E_{i,x}^s\supseteq E_{j,x}^s; $ \item[(3)] $ E_{i,x}^u \oplus E_{i,x}^s=T_xM$, for any $x\in\mathcal O(Z_i) $; \item[(4)] if $x\in Z_i$, $v^s\in E_{i,x}^s$, and $v^u\in E_{i,x}^u$, then $$ |Df(x)v^s|_*\leq\theta|v^s|_*, \qquad |D(f^{-1})(x)v^u|_*\leq\theta|v^u|_*. $$ \end{itemize} Here $ \mathcal O^+(Z)=\bigcup_{n\geq0}f^n(Z)$, $\mathcal O^-(Z)=\bigcup_{n\leq0}f^n(Z)$, $\mathcal O(Z)=\mathcal O^+(Z)\cup\mathcal O^-(Z) $. The one-step estimates in item~(4) are asserted for $x\in Z_i$, not for all $x\in\mathcal O(Z_i)$. \end{statement} The following uniform consequences are stated immediately after the proof of Proposition~7.1 in \cite[p.~66]{Robinson1976}. We label them (5) and (6) for use below; they are unnumbered in Robinson's paper. \begin{statement}[Uniform estimates following Proposition~7.1] Let $\{\gamma_i\}_{i=1}^m$ be a $C^{\infty}$ partition of unity subordinate to the finite open cover $\{\mathcal O(Z_i)\}_{i=1}^m$. There exists an integer $q\geq0$ such that, for every $i$ and every $x\in\mathrm{supp}\gamma_i$, \begin{itemize} \item the forward orbit of $x$ lies in $\bigcup_{j\geq i}Z_j$ except at most $q$ iterates; \item the backward orbit of $x$ lies in $\bigcup_{j\leq i}Z_j$ except at most $q$ iterates. \end{itemize} Set $ b_*:=\sup_{x\in M}\max\left\{\|Df(x)\|_*,\|D(f^{-1})(x)\|_*\right\}$, $C_*:=\frac{b_*^q}{\theta^q}. $ Then: \begin{itemize} \item[(5)] for every $x\in\mathrm{supp}\gamma_i$, $n\geq0$, $v^s\in E_{i,x}^s$, and $v^u\in E_{i,x}^u$, \begin{equation} |Df^n(x)v^s|_*\leq C_*\theta^n|v^s|_*, \qquad |D(f^{-n})(x)v^u|_*\leq C_*\theta^n|v^u|_*; \end{equation} \item[(6)] the stable and unstable bundles are uniformly transverse on $\operatorname{supp}\gamma_i$. Consequently, there exists $C_{\mathrm{proj},*}>0$, independent of $i$ and $x$, such that the projections \[ \pi_{i,x}^s:T_xM\to E_{i,x}^s \quad\text{along }E_{i,x}^u, \qquad \pi_{i,x}^u:T_xM\to E_{i,x}^u \quad\text{along }E_{i,x}^s \] satisfy $ \|\pi_{i,x}^s\|_*, \|\pi_{i,x}^u\|_* \leq C_{\mathrm{proj},*}$, for $x\in\operatorname{supp}\gamma_i. $ \end{itemize} \end{statement} Indeed, compatibility allows item~(4) of Proposition~\ref{stat:Robinson-bundles} to be applied at every nonexceptional iterate. At each of the at most $q$ exceptional iterates, the norm increases by at most $b_*$. Hence $ b_*^q\theta^{n-q}=C_*\theta^n, $ which gives item~(5). Item~(6) follows from continuity of the bundles, compactness of $\mathrm{supp}\gamma_i$, and finiteness of the family.
nodes.statement_short: Robinson's compatible bundles and their uniform estimates.

nodes.name: Robinson's Proposition 7.1
nodes.statement: \textbf{Compatible bundles.} Let $ \Omega(f)=\Omega_1\cup\cdots\cup\Omega_m $ be the spectral decomposition. In the notation of this paper, Proposition~7.1 of \cite[p.~66]{Robinson1976} gives the following statement with respect to the adapted metric. \begin{statement}[Robinson, Proposition~7.1] There exist neighborhoods $Z_i$ of $\Omega_i$, continuous subbundles $E_i^u,E_i^s$ of $TM|_{\mathcal O(Z_i)}$, $i=1,\ldots,m$, and $\theta\in(0,1)$ such that: \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] $E_i^u$ and $E_i^s$ are invariant under $Df$; \item[(2)] if $x\in\mathcal O^+(Z_j)\cap\mathcal O^-(Z_i)$, then $ E_{i,x}^u\subseteq E_{j,x}^u$, $E_{i,x}^s\supseteq E_{j,x}^s; $ \item[(3)] $ E_{i,x}^u \oplus E_{i,x}^s=T_xM$, for any $x\in\mathcal O(Z_i) $; \item[(4)] if $x\in Z_i$, $v^s\in E_{i,x}^s$, and $v^u\in E_{i,x}^u$, then $$ |Df(x)v^s|_*\leq\theta|v^s|_*, \qquad |D(f^{-1})(x)v^u|_*\leq\theta|v^u|_*. $$ \end{itemize} Here $ \mathcal O^+(Z)=\bigcup_{n\geq0}f^n(Z)$, $\mathcal O^-(Z)=\bigcup_{n\leq0}f^n(Z)$, $\mathcal O(Z)=\mathcal O^+(Z)\cup\mathcal O^-(Z) $. The one-step estimates in item~(4) are asserted for $x\in Z_i$, not for all $x\in\mathcal O(Z_i)$. \end{statement}
nodes.statement_short: Quote Robinson's Proposition 7.1.

nodes.name: Uniform consequences
nodes.statement: The following uniform consequences are stated immediately after the proof of Proposition~7.1 in \cite[p.~66]{Robinson1976}. We label them (5) and (6) for use below; they are unnumbered in Robinson's paper. \begin{statement}[Uniform estimates following Proposition~7.1] Let $\{\gamma_i\}_{i=1}^m$ be a $C^{\infty}$ partition of unity subordinate to the finite open cover $\{\mathcal O(Z_i)\}_{i=1}^m$. There exists an integer $q\geq0$ such that, for every $i$ and every $x\in\mathrm{supp}\gamma_i$, \begin{itemize} \item the forward orbit of $x$ lies in $\bigcup_{j\geq i}Z_j$ except at most $q$ iterates; \item the backward orbit of $x$ lies in $\bigcup_{j\leq i}Z_j$ except at most $q$ iterates. \end{itemize} Set $ b_*:=\sup_{x\in M}\max\left\{\|Df(x)\|_*,\|D(f^{-1})(x)\|_*\right\}$, $C_*:=\frac{b_*^q}{\theta^q}. $ Then: \begin{itemize} \item[(5)] for every $x\in\mathrm{supp}\gamma_i$, $n\geq0$, $v^s\in E_{i,x}^s$, and $v^u\in E_{i,x}^u$, \begin{equation} |Df^n(x)v^s|_*\leq C_*\theta^n|v^s|_*, \qquad |D(f^{-n})(x)v^u|_*\leq C_*\theta^n|v^u|_*; \end{equation} \item[(6)] the stable and unstable bundles are uniformly transverse on $\operatorname{supp}\gamma_i$. Consequently, there exists $C_{\mathrm{proj},*}>0$, independent of $i$ and $x$, such that the projections \[ \pi_{i,x}^s:T_xM\to E_{i,x}^s \quad\text{along }E_{i,x}^u, \qquad \pi_{i,x}^u:T_xM\to E_{i,x}^u \quad\text{along }E_{i,x}^s \] satisfy $ \|\pi_{i,x}^s\|_*, \|\pi_{i,x}^u\|_* \leq C_{\mathrm{proj},*}$, for $x\in\operatorname{supp}\gamma_i. $ \end{itemize} \end{statement} Indeed, compatibility allows item~(4) of Proposition~\ref{stat:Robinson-bundles} to be applied at every nonexceptional iterate. At each of the at most $q$ exceptional iterates, the norm increases by at most $b_*$. Hence $ b_*^q\theta^{n-q}=C_*\theta^n, $ which gives item~(5). Item~(6) follows from continuity of the bundles, compactness of $\mathrm{supp}\gamma_i$, and finiteness of the family.
nodes.statement_short: Quote and justify the uniform estimates (5)-(6).

nodes.name: Estimate (5)
nodes.statement: Indeed, compatibility allows item~(4) of Proposition~\ref{stat:Robinson-bundles} to be applied at every nonexceptional iterate. At each of the at most $q$ exceptional iterates, the norm increases by at most $b_*$. Hence $ b_*^q\theta^{n-q}=C_*\theta^n, $ which gives item~(5).
nodes.statement_short: One-step contraction except at q exceptional iterates gives C_* theta^n.

nodes.name: Estimate (6)
nodes.statement: Item~(6) follows from continuity of the bundles, compactness of $\mathrm{supp}\gamma_i$, and finiteness of the family.
nodes.statement_short: Transversality from continuity, compactness and finiteness.

nodes.name: Return to original metric
nodes.statement: \textbf{Return to the original metric.} By \eqref{eq:app-equivalent-metrics}, items~(5)--(6) remain valid in the original metric after replacing their constants by $ C_1:=\kappa^2\max\{C_*,C_{\mathrm{proj},*}\}. $ Thus, for $x\in\mathrm{supp}\gamma_i$, $n\geq0$, $v^s\in E_{i,x}^s$, and $v^u\in E_{i,x}^u$, \begin{equation} |Df^n(x)v^s|_0\leq C_1\theta^n|v^s|_0, \quad |D(f^{-n})(x)v^u|_0\leq C_1\theta^n|v^u|_0, \quad \|\pi_{i,x}^s\|_0,\|\pi_{i,x}^u\|_0\leq C_1. \end{equation} Consequently, all constants in the compatible-bundle construction are uniform in the original metric. Together with the orbitwise gluing in the Robbin--Robinson construction, this yields Proposition~\ref{stat:uniform-CL-finite}; see also \cite[p.~277, after Definition~3]{PilCL}.
nodes.statement_short: Constants transfer to the original metric, yielding the proposition.

nodes.name: Axiom A implies GH
nodes.statement: Assume first that $f$ satisfies Axiom~A and the strong transversality condition. By Proposition~\ref{stat:uniform-CL-finite}, every derivative sequence admits a $(C_0,\lambda_0)$-structure, with constants independent of the trajectory. On $\Omega(f)$, use the ordinary hyperbolic splitting $ TM|_{\Omega(f)}=E_\Omega^s\oplus E_\Omega^u, $ whose exponential estimates and projection bounds are uniform; denote corresponding constants by $C_\Omega>0$ and $\lambda_\Omega\in(0,1)$. The invariant set $M\setminus\Omega(f)$ contains no periodic points. Choose one representative $p$ from each orbit in this set and write a chosen $(C_0,\lambda_0)$-structure along its derivative sequence as \[ T_{f^k(p)}M=E_k^s\oplus E_k^u,\qquad k\in\mathbb{Z}. \] Define $ E_{f^k(p)}^s:=E_k^s$, $E_{f^k(p)}^u:=E_k^u. $ These definitions are unambiguous because the orbit is nonperiodic. On $\Omega(f)$, set $ E_x^s=E_{\Omega,x}^s$, $ E_x^u=E_{\Omega,x}^u. $ With $ C=\max\{C_0,C_\Omega\}, $ $ \lambda=\max\{\lambda_0,\lambda_\Omega\}, $ the associated projections satisfy {\rm(GH1)}--{\rm(GH3)} on $M$. No continuity of the projections is required.
nodes.statement_short: Build a GH splitting from Axiom A and strong transversality.

nodes.name: Uniform orbit structures
nodes.statement: Assume first that $f$ satisfies Axiom~A and the strong transversality condition. By Proposition~\ref{stat:uniform-CL-finite}, every derivative sequence admits a $(C_0,\lambda_0)$-structure, with constants independent of the trajectory.
nodes.statement_short: Every derivative sequence has a uniform (C_0,lambda_0)-structure.

nodes.name: Splitting on Omega
nodes.statement: On $\Omega(f)$, use the ordinary hyperbolic splitting $ TM|_{\Omega(f)}=E_\Omega^s\oplus E_\Omega^u, $ whose exponential estimates and projection bounds are uniform; denote corresponding constants by $C_\Omega>0$ and $\lambda_\Omega\in(0,1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Use the hyperbolic splitting on the nonwandering set.

nodes.name: Glue off Omega
nodes.statement: The invariant set $M\setminus\Omega(f)$ contains no periodic points. Choose one representative $p$ from each orbit in this set and write a chosen $(C_0,\lambda_0)$-structure along its derivative sequence as \[ T_{f^k(p)}M=E_k^s\oplus E_k^u,\qquad k\in\mathbb{Z}. \] Define $ E_{f^k(p)}^s:=E_k^s$, $E_{f^k(p)}^u:=E_k^u. $ These definitions are unambiguous because the orbit is nonperiodic. On $\Omega(f)$, set $ E_x^s=E_{\Omega,x}^s$, $ E_x^u=E_{\Omega,x}^u. $ With $ C=\max\{C_0,C_\Omega\}, $ $ \lambda=\max\{\lambda_0,\lambda_\Omega\}, $ the associated projections satisfy {\rm(GH1)}--{\rm(GH3)} on $M$. No continuity of the projections is required.
nodes.statement_short: Choose one structure per wandering orbit and glue; GH1-GH3 hold.

nodes.name: GH implies Axiom A
nodes.statement: Conversely, assume that $f$ satisfies generalized hyperbolicity. Condition {\rm(GH3)} gives $ E_p^s\subseteq B^+(p)$, $E_p^u\subseteq B^-(p). $ Therefore, \[ T_pM=E_p^s\oplus E_p^u \subseteq B^+(p)+B^-(p) \subseteq T_pM, \] and hence \eqref{eq:app-Mane} holds. By Theorem~\ref{thm:app-Mane}, $f$ is structurally stable. The $C^1$ stability theorem \cite{Mane1987} then implies Axiom~A and the strong transversality condition.
nodes.statement_short: GH gives Mañé's criterion, hence structural stability and Axiom A with strong transversality.

nodes.name: (P1)
nodes.statement: {\rm(P1)} For $f_1, f_2 \in \mathfrak{D}(\mathbb{B})$ the chain rule gives $\|D(f_1 \circ f_2)(x)\| \leq R_1R_2$ and $ \|D(f_1 \circ f_2)(x+v) - D(f_1 \circ f_2)(x)\| \leq R_1 r_2(|v|) + R_2 r_1(R_2|v|), $ so $f_1 \circ f_2 \in \mathfrak{D}(\mathbb{B})$; in particular $g \in \mathfrak{D}(\mathbb{B})$. The spaces $\tilde E^{s,u}_x = Dh(h^{-1}(x))E^{s,u}_{h^{-1}(x)}$ satisfy {\rm(GH1)}--{\rm(GH3)} for $g$ with constants $R_h^2C$ and $\lambda$.
nodes.statement_short: Chain rule closes D(B) under composition; transported splitting for the conjugate.

nodes.name: (P2)
nodes.statement: {\rm(P2)} The two inclusions in {\rm(GH2)} and the two estimates in {\rm(GH3)} interchange under $f \to f^{-1}$, $E^s_x \leftrightarrow E^u_x$.
nodes.statement_short: Inverting f swaps the inclusions and estimates.

nodes.name: (P3)
nodes.statement: {\rm(P3)} Conditions {\rm(GH1)}, {\rm(GH2)} are preserved by iteration, and $|Df^{nm}(x)v^s| \leq C\lambda^{nm}|v^s| = C(\lambda^n)^m|v^s|$.
nodes.statement_short: Iteration preserves GH with rate lambda^n.

nodes.name: (P4)
nodes.statement: {\rm(P4)} Since $f_i(0) = 0$ and $\|Df_i\| \leq R$, we have $|f_i(x_i)| \leq R|x_i|$, so $f$ maps $\mathbb{B}$ into $\mathbb{B}$; the same applies to $f^{-1}$. Since $r$ is nondecreasing and $|v_i| \leq \|v\|$, $$ \bigl\|\{f_i(x_i+v_i) - f_i(x_i) - Df_i(x_i)v_i\}\bigr\| \leq r(\|v\|)\|v\|, $$ $$ \|Df(x+v) - Df(x)\| = \sup_i \|Df_i(x_i+v_i) - Df_i(x_i)\| \leq r(\|v\|), $$ hence $f \in \mathfrak{D}(\mathbb{B})$ and $Df(x) = \bigoplus_i Df_i(x_i)$. The projections $P_x = \bigoplus_i P^{(i)}_{x_i}$ and $Q_x = \bigoplus_i Q^{(i)}_{x_i}$ are diagonal, so $\|P_x\| = \sup_i \|P^{(i)}_{x_i}\| \leq C$, and {\rm(GH2)}, {\rm(GH3)} hold coordinatewise.
nodes.statement_short: Coordinatewise bounds give the product in D(B) with diagonal projections.
